What it does show is a teacher who answers a question about life with the law's first command and a call to do it — the pattern of 6:46 and 8:21 in this reconstruction, and of the Epistle of James ("be doers of the word", Jas 1:22).
The reading of this text: seventy, without "two".
The narrator's name for Jesus, as at 7:13.
To show forth, designate.
A Hebrew idiom for "ahead of him", kept as at 9:52.

notes.term: τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ, "the lord of the harvest"
notes.explanation: The owner of the harvest. Lower case: the image is of a landowner.
ἐκβάλλω, the verb used for driving out daimons (9:40). "Send out" softens it.
δέομαι, to ask out of need.
Greetings on the road were long and formal.
A Semitic idiom: one who belongs to peace.
To come to rest on.
As at 6:23.
Those without strength, the sick.
A perfect: it has drawn near and is near.
To wipe off, as one wipes off something unclean.
To set aside, treat as nothing, reject.
To be placed under, to submit.
ὄφις, serpent, snake.
A double negative, the strongest Greek denial.
To do wrong to, injure.
A perfect: written in, and standing written.
Plural, as the Greek has it.
To leap for joy, exult.
The reading of this text. Canonical Luke has ἐξομολογοῦμαι, "I acknowledge, praise".
Addressed to God, so capitalised. This text lacks "Father" before it and "and of earth" after it.

notes.term: ἅτινα ἦν κρυπτά… ἀπεκάλυψας, "what was hidden… you revealed"
notes.explanation: The reading of this text: things that were hidden. Canonical Luke has "you hid these things… and revealed them".
Literally "not yet speaking": babies, the simple.
The nominative with the article used as an address, word for word.
Good pleasure, what seems good.
παραδίδωμι, as at 9:44.
Lower case, as the Greek has no capitals.
To will, decide.
One skilled in the law of Moses.

notes.term: ἀνέστη ἐκπειράζων, "stood up, putting him to the test"
notes.explanation: ἀνίστημι; ἐκπειράζω, to test thoroughly.
The reading of this text, "life" alone. Canonical Luke has "life of the age".
To receive as one's lot or share.
Literally that: how do you read it?

notes.term: κύριον τὸν θεόν σου, "the Lord your God"
notes.explanation: Quoting Deut 6:5. κύριος stands for the divine name, so it is capitalised.

notes.term: ἐξ… καὶ ἐν…, "out of… and with…"
notes.explanation: The Greek changes the preposition after the first member.
Understanding, the thinking mind.
Literally "the one near".

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 9
chapters.preamble:
It starts with asking how to ask. The prayer given here wants the spirit first, then the kingdom, then bread enough for the day, and it lets go of what is owed to us as readily as it asks to be let go.

Asking turns out to be a matter of knocking at midnight on a door already shut for the night, and going on knocking without shame. Nothing that answers from inside will hand us a snake.

Then something that has kept us mute goes out, and we speak, and at once part of us suspects the cure. A strong one guards its courtyard and all its goods are at peace, until a stronger one comes.

The chapter ends at a table, before a cup polished on the outside. We clean what can be seen, count out our tenths of mint and rue, sit in the first seats, and keep hold of a key we never use.

Whoever made the outside made the inside as well.

verses.english: And it happened, while he was praying in a certain place, that when he stopped, one of his learners said to him, "Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his learners."
verses.greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν τόπῳ τινὶ προσευχόμενον, ὡς ἐπαύσατο, εἶπέν τις τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν· Κύριε, δίδαξον ἡμᾶς προσεύχεσθαι, καθὼς καὶ Ἰωάννης ἐδίδαξεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And he said to them, "When you pray, say: Father, let your holy spirit come; let your kingdom come.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὅταν προσεύχησθε, λέγετε· Πάτερ, ἐλθέτω τὸ πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἅγιον· ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου·

verses.english: Your bread for the coming day keep giving us day by day.
verses.greek: τὸν ἄρτον σου τὸν ἐπιούσιον δίδου ἡμῖν τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν·

verses.english: And let go our sins for us, for we ourselves also let go for everyone who owes us. And do not bring us into testing."
verses.greek: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ ἀφίομεν παντὶ ὀφείλοντι ἡμῖν· καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν.

verses.english: And he said to them, "Which of you will have a friend, and will go to him at midnight and say to him, 'Friend, lend me three loaves,
verses.greek: Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἕξει φίλον καὶ πορεύσεται πρὸς αὐτὸν μεσονυκτίου καὶ εἴπῃ αὐτῷ· Φίλε, χρῆσόν μοι τρεῖς ἄρτους,

verses.english: since a friend of mine has arrived to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him';
verses.greek: ἐπειδὴ φίλος μου παρεγένετο ἐξ ὁδοῦ πρός με καὶ οὐκ ἔχω ὃ παραθήσω αὐτῷ·

verses.english: and that one, answering from inside, will say, 'Do not give me trouble; the door has already been shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot get up and give to you'?
verses.greek: κἀκεῖνος ἔσωθεν ἀποκριθεὶς εἴπῃ· Μή μοι κόπους πάρεχε· ἤδη ἡ θύρα κέκλεισται, καὶ τὰ παιδία μου μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὴν κοίτην εἰσίν· οὐ δύναμαι ἀναστὰς δοῦναί σοι.

verses.english: I tell you, even if he will not get up and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his shamelessness he will rouse himself and give him as much as he needs.
verses.greek: λέγω ὑμῖν, εἰ καὶ οὐ δώσει αὐτῷ ἀναστὰς διὰ τὸ εἶναι φίλον αὐτοῦ, διά γε τὴν ἀναίδειαν αὐτοῦ ἐγερθεὶς δώσει αὐτῷ ὅσων χρῄζει.

verses.english: And I say to you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
verses.greek: Κἀγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν·

verses.english: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
verses.greek: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει, καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει, καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.

verses.english: And which of you who is a father, if the son asks for a fish, will instead of a fish hand him a snake?
verses.greek: τίνα δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν τὸν πατέρα αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς ἰχθύν, καὶ ἀντὶ ἰχθύος ὄφιν αὐτῷ ἐπιδώσει;

verses.english: Or if he asks for an egg, will hand him a scorpion?
verses.greek: ἢ καὶ αἰτήσει ᾠόν, ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ σκορπίον;

verses.english: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father who is from heaven give holy spirit to those who ask him!"
verses.greek: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὑπάρχοντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ δώσει πνεῦμα ἅγιον τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.

verses.english: And he was throwing out a daimon, and it was mute; and it happened, when the daimon had gone out, that the mute man spoke; and the crowds marvelled.
verses.greek: Καὶ ἦν ἐκβάλλων δαιμόνιον καὶ αὐτὸ ἦν κωφόν· ἐγένετο δὲ τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐξελθόντος ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός. καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι·

verses.english: But some of them said, "By Beelzebul, the ruler of the daimons, he throws out the daimons."
verses.greek: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπον· Ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια·

verses.english: And others, testing him, were seeking from him a sign out of heaven.
verses.greek: ἕτεροι δὲ πειράζοντες σημεῖον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐζήτουν παρ’ αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls upon house.
verses.greek: αὐτὸς δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὰ διανοήματα εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν διαμερισθεῖσα ἐρημοῦται, καὶ οἶκος ἐπὶ οἶκον πίπτει.

verses.english: And if Satan too has been divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? Because you say that I throw out the daimons by Beelzebul.
verses.greek: εἰ δὲ καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν διεμερίσθη, πῶς σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ; ὅτι λέγετε ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλειν με τὰ δαιμόνια.

verses.english: But if I throw out the daimons by Beelzebul, your sons, by whom do they throw them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
verses.greek: εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν; διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ ὑμῶν κριταὶ ἔσονται.

verses.english: But if I throw out the daimons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has arrived upon you.
verses.greek: εἰ δὲ ἐν δακτύλῳ θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: When the strong one, fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his possessions are in peace;
verses.greek: ὅταν ὁ ἰσχυρὸς καθωπλισμένος φυλάσσῃ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ αὐλήν, ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἐστὶν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ·

verses.english: but when one stronger than he comes upon him and conquers him, he takes away his full armour, on which he had relied, and distributes his spoils.
verses.greek: ἐπὰν δὲ ἰσχυρότερος αὐτοῦ ἐπελθὼν νικήσῃ αὐτόν, τὴν πανοπλίαν αὐτοῦ αἴρει ἐφ’ ᾗ ἐπεποίθει, καὶ τὰ σκῦλα αὐτοῦ διαδίδωσιν.

verses.english: The one who is not with me is against me, and the one who does not gather with me scatters."
verses.greek: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.

verses.english: And it happened, as he was saying these things, that a certain woman from the crowd, raising her voice, said to him, "Fortunate is the womb that carried you, and the breasts that you sucked!"
verses.greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις φωνὴν γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας·

verses.english: But he said, "Rather, fortunate are those who hear the word of God and keep it."
verses.greek: αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν· Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσοντες.

verses.english: And as the crowds were gathering thickly, he began to say, "This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, and a sign will not be given to it."
verses.greek: Τῶν δὲ ὄχλων ἐπαθροιζομένων ἤρξατο λέγειν· Ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη γενεὰ πονηρά ἐστιν· σημεῖον ζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ.

verses.english: "No one, having lit a lamp, puts it in a hidden place, nor under the measuring basket, but on the lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light."
verses.greek: Οὐδεὶς λύχνον ἅψας εἰς κρύπτην τίθησιν οὐδὲ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι τὸ φῶς βλέπωσιν.

verses.english: And as he was speaking, a Pharisee asks him to have the midday meal with him; and going in, he reclined at table.
verses.greek: Ἐν δὲ τῷ λαλῆσαι ἐρωτᾷ αὐτὸν Φαρισαῖος ὅπως ἀριστήσῃ παρ’ αὐτῷ· εἰσελθὼν δὲ ἀνέπεσεν.

verses.english: And the Pharisee began, debating within himself, to say: why was he not first washed before the meal?
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Φαρισαῖος ἤρξατο διακρινόμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγειν διὰ τί οὐ πρῶτον ἐβαπτίσθη πρὸ τοῦ ἀρίστου.

verses.english: But the lord said to him, "Now you, the Pharisees, cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but your inside is full of plunder and evil.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· Νῦν ὑμεῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τοῦ πίνακος καθαρίζετε, τὸ δὲ ἔσωθεν ὑμῶν γέμει ἁρπαγῆς καὶ πονηρίας.

verses.english: Senseless ones! Did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?
verses.greek: ἄφρονες, οὐχ ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔξωθεν καὶ τὸ ἔσωθεν ἐποίησεν;

verses.english: But give what is inside as a gift of mercy, and look, all things are clean for you.
verses.greek: πλὴν τὰ ἐνόντα δότε ἐλεημοσύνην, καὶ ἰδοὺ πάντα καθαρὰ ὑμῖν ἐστιν.

verses.english: But woe to you, the Pharisees, because you take a tenth of the mint and the rue and every garden herb, and pass by the calling and the love of God. But these you ought to have done, and not to have let the others go.
verses.greek: Ἀλλὰ οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ πήγανον καὶ πᾶν λάχανον, καὶ παρέρχεσθε τὴν κλῆσιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ· ταῦτα δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ παρεῖναι.

verses.english: Woe to you, the Pharisees, because you love the first seat in the assemblies and the greetings in the marketplaces.
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀγαπᾶτε τὴν πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς.

verses.english: Woe to you, because you are like the tombs that are not seen, and the people walking over them do not know it."
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι ἐστὲ ὡς τὰ μνημεῖα τὰ ἄδηλα, καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ περιπατοῦντες ἐπάνω οὐκ οἴδασιν.

verses.english: And one of the experts in the law answers and says to him, "Teacher, saying these things you insult us too."
verses.greek: Ἀποκριθεὶς δέ τις τῶν νομικῶν λέγει αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα λέγων καὶ ἡμᾶς ὑβρίζεις.

verses.english: But he said, "Woe to you, the experts in the law, too, because you load the people with loads hard to carry, and you yourselves do not touch the loads with one of your fingers.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς οὐαί, ὅτι φορτίζετε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους φορτία δυσβάστακτα, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἑνὶ τῶν δακτύλων ὑμῶν οὐ προσψαύετε τοῖς φορτίοις.

verses.english: Woe to you, because you build the tombs of the prophets, but your fathers killed them.
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν προφητῶν οἱ δὲ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτούς.

verses.english: So you are witnesses, and consent to the works of your fathers, because they killed them, and you build.
verses.greek: ἄρα μάρτυρές ἐστε καὶ συνευδοκεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν, ὅτι αὐτοὶ μὲν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτοὺς ὑμεῖς δὲ οἰκοδομεῖτε.

verses.english: Woe to you, the experts in the law, because you took away the key of knowledge; you yourselves did not go in, and those going in you hindered."
verses.greek: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς, ὅτι ἤρατε τὴν κλεῖδα τῆς γνώσεως· αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσήλθατε καὶ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἐκωλύσατε.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.26.1–5 does not quote the prayer. He turns each petition into a question about which God it is addressed to, in the order of the prayer, and then says "in this order" (hoc ordine): "To whom shall I say, Father?… From whom shall I ask the holy spirit?… Whose kingdom shall I wish to come?… Who will give me daily bread?… Who will forgive me my sins?… Who will not let us be led into temptation?" There is no question about the hallowing of the name. The text therefore asked for the holy spirit where canonical Luke has "hallowed be your name", and kept "your kingdom come". Tertullian does not give the wording of the request for the spirit. The Greek printed takes the form of the only Greek witnesses with such a petition in Luke (minuscules 700 and 162, Gregory of Nyssa), shortened to what Tertullian attests. In those witnesses it replaces "your kingdom come"; here it stands beside it. Origen quotes the bread petition of "those from Marcion" in Greek: "your bread" (τὸν ἄρτον σου), not "our bread". He asks them "what is the bread of God?" ἐπιούσιος is translated "for the coming day"; Tertullian has "daily" (cotidianum).

notes.term: The holy spirit asked and given (11:2, 11:13)
notes.explanation: Interpretation. In this text the prayer opens with a request for the holy spirit, and the teaching that follows ends with the Father who will "give holy spirit to those who ask him" (11:13; Tertullian 4.26.10). The unit begins and ends with the spirit. The bread asked for is the Father's ("your bread"), and Origen's question to the Marcionites, "what is the bread of God?", shows that they read it as more than food. This is the reception, and the text does not settle that reading. What the text itself shows is a prayer centred on receiving from the Father. The library reads such receiving as influx into a vessel (The River and the Vessel).

Epiphanius, sch. 24 quotes 11:5, 11:9a and 11:11–13 in one scholion; Tertullian, Marc. 4.26.5–10 alludes to the friend at midnight, the door already shut with the children in bed, the request granted because of persistence, the asking, seeking and knocking, and the snake and scorpion. Neither witness has the pair "bread and stone" that most manuscripts add at 11:11 (it is also absent in 𝔓45, 𝔓75 and B). 11:6 and 11:10 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.26.10–12 quotes "If I cast out daimons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out?" and "If I by the finger of God cast out daimons, has the kingdom of God not come near to you?" He points out that the Egyptian magicians called the Creator's power "the finger of God" (Exod 8:19), and that the stronger man of the parable overcomes the prince of daimons. NA27 prints [καὶ αὐτὸ ἦν] at 11:14 and [ἐγώ] at 11:20 in brackets; both are printed (SBLGNT omits them). 11:16–17 and 11:23 are not cited and are printed in grey. The return of the unclean spirit (11:24–26), a paragraph that no witness cites, is not printed.

Epiphanius, sch. 25: "he cut out what is about Jonah the prophet; for he had 'this generation — a sign will not be given to it'; he did not have what is about Nineveh and the queen of the south and Solomon." Tertullian: Christ "does not give a sign to those who ask" (4.27.1). The saying in this text ends "a sign will not be given to it". Canonical Luke adds "except the sign of Jonah" and the sayings on the Ninevites and the queen of the south (11:30–32, Matthew 12:39–42). The verbs "he cut" are Epiphanius' charge. What they report as content is that the words were not there.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.27.2–5. The Pharisee "was debating within himself why he had not first been washed before reclining, according to the law". That is the reading of codex D and the Old Latin, and it is printed in D's Greek. Canonical Luke has the Pharisee "amazed". Jesus' reply on the outside and inside of the cup, "Did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?", is glossed by Tertullian as flesh and soul made by one God. At 11:42 both witnesses read that the Pharisees pass over "the calling (κλῆσις) and the love of God", not "justice (κρίσις) and the love of God"; Tertullian repeats "calling" in 4.27.6. The reading is printed. 11:44 is not cited and is printed in grey.

notes.term: Woes on the experts in the law (11:45–52; 11:49–51 not printed)
notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.27.6–9; Epiphanius, sch. 27–28. The experts in the law load others with burdens hard to bear; they build the tombs of the prophets their fathers killed; they have taken the key of knowledge (Tertullian: "the interpretation of the law"). Epiphanius states that the text did not have the saying "Therefore the wisdom of God said, 'I will send them prophets…'" or the blood of the prophets from Abel to Zechariah "required of this generation" (11:49–51). At 11:48 Tertullian's comment ("they testified that they did not consent to the deeds of their fathers") agrees with the reading of D, "you testify that you do not approve"; it is not a quotation and is recorded, not adopted. 11:45 is not cited and is printed in grey. 11:53–54 form a paragraph that no witness cites and are not printed.

Interpretation. In the attested text the charge against the Pharisees is that they tithe herbs and pass over "the calling and the love of God". Tertullian reads "calling" as God calling Israel out of Egypt and "love" as the first commandment (Deut 6:5), quoted in that form (4.27.4). The pairing fits the reconstruction's earlier sayings: the expert in the law is answered with the command to love God (10:27). It also fits a criticism of religious leaders made from within the law, for neglecting what the law puts first.
"Lord, sir": the capital is only the start of the address.
The address, without "our" and without "who are in the heavens".

notes.term: ἐλθέτω τὸ πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἅγιον, "let your holy spirit come"
notes.explanation: The petition of this text, in place of canonical Luke's "let your name be held holy". Its exact wording is not given by the witnesses. Manuscript 700 and Gregory of Nyssa read it with "upon us, and let it cleanse us"; those words are not printed and are not translated.
A third-person imperative: "let it come". "May it come" softens it into a wish.
The reading of this text, "your" (God's) bread. Canonical Luke has "our bread".

The word occurs almost nowhere outside this prayer, and its meaning is not known for certain. Proposals: "for the coming day" (from ἡ ἐπιοῦσα, "the next day"), "needed for existence" (from οὐσία, "being"), and "supersubstantial", the Latin of Jerome. The first fits "day by day" and is the most likely; the others are possible.

notes.term: δίδου… τὸ καθ' ἡμέραν, "keep giving… day by day"
notes.explanation: A present imperative: give, and go on giving.

notes.term: ἄφες… ἀφίομεν, "let go… we let go"
notes.explanation: ἀφίημι, as at 5:20. One verb for both: God's letting go and ours.

notes.term: παντὶ ὀφείλοντι ἡμῖν, "everyone who owes us"
notes.explanation: A debtor. The prayer's own image is of debts released.
πειρασμός is a test, a trial, a putting to the proof. "Temptation", an enticement to sin, is one kind of testing.
To lend.
Labour, bother.

ἀναίδεια means shamelessness, a lack of shame. "Persistence" is not what the word means. Whose shamelessness is not quite clear: most read it as the asker's, some as the sleeper's wish to avoid shame.
ἀνίστημι and ἐγείρω, both in one sentence.
Present imperatives: keep asking, keep seeking, keep knocking.

notes.term: τίνα… τὸν πατέρα, "which of you who is a father"
notes.explanation: The Greek is loose: "which of you, the father, will the son ask…".
πονηρός, as at 6:45.

notes.term: ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, "the Father who is from heaven"
notes.explanation: ἐξ, "out of, from".
Without the article: "holy spirit", not "the Holy Spirit".
κωφός means both deaf and mute; here, mute.
A Semitic name, probably "lord of the dwelling" or "lord of the height".
ἄρχων, as at 8:41.
Made a desert (ἔρημος).
A Hebrew word, "the adversary", left untranslated in the Greek and here.
φθάνω, to come before, reach, arrive.
The enclosed court of a house.
Undisturbed.
πείθω in the perfect, "to be persuaded, rely on". Not πίστις, "trust".
Arms stripped from a defeated enemy.
As at 6:20.
Literally the belly, the womb.
It corrects or strengthens what was said: "rather", "yes, but".
To guard, keep watch over.

notes.term: σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ, "a sign will not be given to it"
notes.explanation: The reading of this text, without "except the sign of Jonah".
A cellar or vault.
A grain measure.
The present tense in past narration, kept.
ἄριστον, the first meal of the day, taken toward noon.
The reading of this text, with D's Greek.
βαπτίζω, to dip, immerse: a ritual washing before the meal. It is the verb behind "baptiser" (7:20).
As at 7:13.
A dish, a board for food.
Robbery, what is seized. "Greed" weakens it.
Without sense, foolish.
The contents, what is within.
From ἔλεος, mercy: alms.
You tithe.
The reading of this text. Canonical Luke has τὴν κρίσιν, "justice, judgement".
παρίημι, to let pass, neglect.
The seat of honour.
Unmarked, invisible. Contact with a tomb made a person unclean.
The present tense in past narration, kept.
To treat with outrage.
One root, kept as one English word.
Difficult to bear.
To approve together with.

notes.term: κλεῖδα τῆς γνώσεως, "the key of knowledge"
notes.explanation: γνῶσις, knowledge.
To prevent, hold back.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 10
chapters.preamble:
Things whispered in inner rooms do not stay there. Whatever we said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what threatens us from outside can only kill what is outside.

Part of us has a good harvest. It tells its soul that it has plenty laid up for years to come, and that it can rest. That night the soul is asked for back.

Look instead at the ravens, which have no storeroom, and the lilies, which do no work and are clothed better than the richest king. The kingdom has already been given. It does not have to be stored.

What is asked of us is to stay awake: belts fastened, lamps lit, listening for a knock. Whatever is found awake will be served at table by the master himself. Whatever decides the master is late, and starts beating the others, will not be ready.

Then fire, and a division running through the house. We read the face of the sky without difficulty. We cannot read the time we are in.

verses.english: Meanwhile, when the tens of thousands of the crowd had gathered together, so that they were trampling one another, he began to say to his learners first, "Keep yourselves away from the leaven of the Pharisees, which is play-acting.
verses.greek: Ἐν οἷς ἐπισυναχθεισῶν τῶν μυριάδων τοῦ ὄχλου, ὥστε καταπατεῖν ἀλλήλους, ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ πρῶτον· Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης, ἥτις ἐστὶν ὑπόκρισις, τῶν Φαρισαίων.

verses.english: And nothing is covered over that will not be uncovered, and hidden that will not be known.
verses.greek: οὐδὲν δὲ συγκεκαλυμμένον ἐστὶν ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.

verses.english: Because of this, whatever you said in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what you spoke into the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed upon the roofs.
verses.greek: ἀνθ’ ὧν ὅσα ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτὶ ἀκουσθήσεται, καὶ ὃ πρὸς τὸ οὖς ἐλαλήσατε ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις κηρυχθήσεται ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.

verses.english: And I say to you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after these things have nothing more they can do.
verses.greek: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν τοῖς φίλοις μου, μὴ φοβηθῆτε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεινόντων τὸ σῶμα καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα μὴ ἐχόντων περισσότερόν τι ποιῆσαι.

verses.english: But I will show you whom you should fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to throw into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear this one.
verses.greek: ὑποδείξω δὲ ὑμῖν τίνα φοβηθῆτε· φοβήθητε τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποκτεῖναι ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν βαλεῖν εἰς γέενναν· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, τοῦτον φοβήθητε.

verses.english: And I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before the humans, the son of the human also will acknowledge him before God;
verses.greek: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, πᾶς ὃς ἂν ὁμολογήσῃ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὁμολογήσει ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θεοῦ·

verses.english: but the one who disowns me before the humans will be disowned before God.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ ἀρνησάμενός με ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρνηθήσεται ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: And everyone who will speak a word against the son of the human, it will be let go for him; but for the one who has blasphemed against the holy spirit, it will not be let go.
verses.greek: καὶ πᾶς ὃς ἐρεῖ λόγον εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ τῷ δὲ εἰς τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα βλασφημήσαντι οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.

verses.english: And when they bring you in before the assemblies and the rulers and the authorities, do not be anxious how or what you should answer in defence, or what you should say;
verses.greek: ὅταν δὲ εἰσφέρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐπὶ τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί ἀπολογήσησθε ἢ τί εἴπητε·

verses.english: for the holy spirit will teach you in that very hour what you must say."
verses.greek: τὸ γὰρ ἅγιον πνεῦμα διδάξει ὑμᾶς ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἃ δεῖ εἰπεῖν.

verses.english: And someone from the crowd said to him, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me."
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δέ τις ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπὲ τῷ ἀδελφῷ μου μερίσασθαι μετ’ ἐμοῦ τὴν κληρονομίαν.

verses.english: But he said to him, "Human, who set me up as judge or divider over you?"
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπε, τίς με κατέστησεν κριτὴν ἢ μεριστὴν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς;

verses.english: And he said to them, "Look, and guard yourselves against every kind of wanting more, because a person's life is not in having more than enough of his possessions."
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁρᾶτε καὶ φυλάσσεσθε ἀπὸ πάσης πλεονεξίας, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν τινὶ ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ.

verses.english: And he spoke a parable to them, saying, "The land of a certain rich man bore well.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων· Ἀνθρώπου τινὸς πλουσίου εὐφόρησεν ἡ χώρα.

verses.english: And he was reasoning within himself, saying, 'What shall I do, because I have nowhere to gather my fruits?'
verses.greek: καὶ διελογίζετο ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Τί ποιήσω, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχω ποῦ συνάξω τοὺς καρπούς μου;

verses.english: And he said, 'This I will do: I will pull down my barns and build bigger ones, and I will gather there all my grain and my good things,
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν· Τοῦτο ποιήσω· καθελῶ μου τὰς ἀποθήκας καὶ μείζονας οἰκοδομήσω, καὶ συνάξω ἐκεῖ πάντα τὸν σῖτον καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά μου,

verses.english: and I will say to my soul: Soul, you have many good things laid up for many years; rest, eat, drink, be glad.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἐρῶ τῇ ψυχῇ μου· Ψυχή, ἔχεις πολλὰ ἀγαθὰ κείμενα εἰς ἔτη πολλά· ἀναπαύου, φάγε, πίε, εὐφραίνου.

verses.english: But God said to him, 'Senseless one, this night they are demanding your soul back from you; and the things you have made ready, whose will they be?'
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ θεός· Ἄφρων, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τὴν ψυχήν σου ἀπαιτοῦσιν ἀπὸ σοῦ· ἃ δὲ ἡτοίμασας, τίνι ἔσται;

verses.english: So is the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God."
verses.greek: οὕτως ὁ θησαυρίζων ἑαυτῷ καὶ μὴ εἰς θεὸν πλουτῶν.

verses.english: And he said to his learners, "For this reason I tell you, do not be anxious for the soul, what you will eat, nor for the body, what you will put on.
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι τί ἐνδύσησθε.

verses.english: For the soul is more than the food, and the body than the clothing.
verses.greek: ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος.

verses.english: Consider the ravens, that they do not sow nor reap; they have no storeroom nor barn, and God feeds them. How much more are you worth than the birds!
verses.greek: κατανοήσατε τοὺς κόρακας ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν, οἷς οὐκ ἔστιν ταμεῖον οὐδὲ ἀποθήκη, καὶ ὁ θεὸς τρέφει αὐτούς· πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμεῖς διαφέρετε τῶν πετεινῶν.

verses.english: And which of you, by being anxious, can add a cubit to his stature?
verses.greek: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ προσθεῖναι πῆχυν;

verses.english: If then you cannot do even the least thing, why are you anxious about the rest?
verses.greek: εἰ οὖν οὐδὲ ἐλάχιστον δύνασθε, τί περὶ τῶν λοιπῶν μεριμνᾶτε;

verses.english: Consider the lilies, how they neither spin nor weave; but I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
verses.greek: κατανοήσατε τὰ κρίνα πῶς οὔτε νήθει οὔτε ὑφαίνει· λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.

verses.english: How much more you, you of little trust.
verses.greek: πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι.

verses.english: And you, do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be held in suspense;
verses.greek: καὶ ὑμεῖς μὴ ζητεῖτε τί φάγητε καὶ τί πίητε, καὶ μὴ μετεωρίζεσθε,

verses.english: for all these things the nations of the world seek after, but your Father knows that you need them.
verses.greek: ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τοῦ κόσμου ἐπιζητοῦσιν, ὑμῶν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ οἶδεν ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων.

verses.english: But seek the kingdom of God, and these things will be added to you.
verses.greek: πλὴν ζητεῖτε τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.

verses.english: Do not be afraid, little flock, because the Father has been well pleased to give you the kingdom.
verses.greek: Μὴ φοβοῦ, τὸ μικρὸν ποίμνιον, ὅτι εὐδόκησεν ὁ πατὴρ δοῦναι ὑμῖν τὴν βασιλείαν.

verses.english: Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning,
verses.greek: Ἔστωσαν ὑμῶν αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι καὶ οἱ λύχνοι καιόμενοι,

verses.english: and you, be like humans waiting for their lord, when he will return from the wedding, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him at once.
verses.greek: καὶ ὑμεῖς ὅμοιοι ἀνθρώποις προσδεχομένοις τὸν κύριον ἑαυτῶν πότε ἀναλύσῃ ἐκ τῶν γάμων, ἵνα ἐλθόντος καὶ κρούσαντος εὐθέως ἀνοίξωσιν αὐτῷ.

verses.english: Fortunate are those slaves whom the lord, when he comes, will find keeping awake. Amen, I tell you that he will gird himself and have them recline at table, and he will come by and serve them.
verses.greek: μακάριοι οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι, οὓς ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος εὑρήσει γρηγοροῦντας· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι περιζώσεται καὶ ἀνακλινεῖ αὐτοὺς καὶ παρελθὼν διακονήσει αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: And if he comes in the evening watch and finds them so, fortunate are those.
verses.greek: κἂν ἐν τῇ ἑσπερινῇ φυλακῇ ἔλθῃ καὶ εὕρῃ οὕτως, μακάριοί εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι.

verses.english: But know this, that if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief is coming, he would not have let his house be dug through.
verses.greek: Τοῦτο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ ὥρᾳ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, οὐκ ἂν ἀφῆκεν διορυχθῆναι τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: You also, be ready, because the son of the human is coming at an hour you do not think."
verses.greek: καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ ὥρᾳ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.

verses.english: And Peter said, "Lord, are you saying this parable to us, or to all as well?"
verses.greek: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Κύριε, πρὸς ἡμᾶς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγεις ἢ καὶ πρὸς πάντας;

verses.english: And the lord said, "Who then is the trustworthy steward, the sensible one, whom the lord will set over his household servants, to give the measure of grain at the right time?
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος· Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς οἰκονόμος, ὁ φρόνιμος, ὃν καταστήσει ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς θεραπείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ διδόναι ἐν καιρῷ τὸ σιτομέτριον;

verses.english: Fortunate is that slave whom his lord, when he comes, will find doing so.
verses.greek: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος, ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει ποιοῦντα οὕτως·

verses.english: Truly I tell you that he will set him over all his possessions.
verses.greek: ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν.

verses.english: But if that slave says in his heart, 'My lord is taking his time in coming,' and begins to beat the slave boys and the slave girls, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
verses.greek: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἔρχεσθαι, καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς παῖδας καὶ τὰς παιδίσκας, ἐσθίειν τε καὶ πίνειν καὶ μεθύσκεσθαι,

verses.english: the lord of that slave will come on a day when he is not expecting and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two, and will put his portion with the untrustworthy.
verses.greek: ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει, καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀπίστων θήσει.

verses.english: But that slave who knew the will of his lord and did not make ready or act according to his will will be beaten with many blows;
verses.greek: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ὁ γνοὺς τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ ἑτοιμάσας ἢ ποιήσας πρὸς τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ δαρήσεται πολλάς·

verses.english: but the one who did not know, and did things deserving blows, will be beaten with few. And everyone to whom much was given, much will be sought from him; and the one to whom they entrusted much, they will ask the more of him.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ μὴ γνοὺς ποιήσας δὲ ἄξια πληγῶν δαρήσεται ὀλίγας. παντὶ δὲ ᾧ ἐδόθη πολύ, πολὺ ζητηθήσεται παρ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ᾧ παρέθεντο πολύ, περισσότερον αἰτήσουσιν αὐτόν.

verses.english: Fire I came to throw upon the earth, and what do I want, if it has already been kindled?
verses.greek: Πῦρ ἦλθον βαλεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τί θέλω εἰ ἤδη ἀνήφθη;

verses.english: And I have an immersion to be immersed in, and how I am held fast until it is completed!
verses.greek: βάπτισμα δὲ ἔχω βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ πῶς συνέχομαι ἕως ὅτου τελεσθῇ.

verses.english: Do you think that I arrived to give peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but rather division.
verses.greek: δοκεῖτε ὅτι εἰρήνην παρεγενόμην δοῦναι ἐν τῇ γῇ; οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλ’ ἢ διαμερισμόν.

verses.english: For from now on there will be five in one house divided, three against two and two against three;
verses.greek: ἔσονται γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν πέντε ἐν ἑνὶ οἴκῳ διαμεμερισμένοι, τρεῖς ἐπὶ δυσὶν καὶ δύο ἐπὶ τρισίν,

verses.english: father will be divided against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against the mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against the mother-in-law."
verses.greek: διαμερισθήσεται πατὴρ ἐπὶ υἱῷ καὶ υἱὸς ἐπὶ πατρί, μήτηρ ἐπὶ θυγατέρα καὶ θυγάτηρ ἐπὶ τὴν μητέρα, πενθερὰ ἐπὶ τὴν νύμφην αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφη ἐπὶ τὴν πενθεράν.

verses.english: And he was also saying to the crowds, "When you see the cloud rising in the west, at once you say, 'A rainstorm is coming,' and so it happens;
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὅταν ἴδητε τὴν νεφέλην ἀνατέλλουσαν ἐπὶ δυσμῶν, εὐθέως λέγετε ὅτι Ὄμβρος ἔρχεται, καὶ γίνεται οὕτως·

verses.english: and when you see the south wind blowing, you say, 'There will be scorching heat,' and it happens.
verses.greek: καὶ ὅταν νότον πνέοντα, λέγετε ὅτι Καύσων ἔσται, καὶ γίνεται.

verses.english: Play-actors! The face of the sky and of the earth you know how to test, but this time, how is it that you do not know how to test it?
verses.greek: ὑποκριταί, τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν, τὸν καιρὸν δὲ τοῦτον πῶς οὐκ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν;

verses.english: And why do you not judge even of yourselves what is just?
verses.greek: Τί δὲ καὶ ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν οὐ κρίνετε τὸ δίκαιον;

verses.english: For as you are going away with your opponent at law before a ruler, on the road make an effort to be released from him, so that he does not drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
verses.greek: ὡς γὰρ ὑπάγεις μετὰ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου σου ἐπ’ ἄρχοντα, ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ δὸς ἐργασίαν ἀπηλλάχθαι ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, μήποτε κατασύρῃ σε πρὸς τὸν κριτήν, καὶ ὁ κριτὴς παραδώσει σε τῷ πράκτορι, καὶ ὁ πράκτωρ σε βαλεῖ εἰς φυλακήν.

verses.english: I tell you, you will not come out from there until you have paid back even the last lepton."
verses.greek: λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως καὶ τὸ ἔσχατον λεπτὸν ἀποδῷς.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.28.1–8 follows the passage closely: the leaven of the Pharisees, nothing hidden that will not be known, "do not fear those who can only kill", "fear him who after killing has power to throw into Gehenna", which he says means the Creator, acknowledging and denying "before God", the sin against the holy spirit, and the spirit teaching in that hour. Epiphanius, sch. 29–30 quotes 12:4–5 in Greek ("to throw into Gehenna", βαλεῖν εἰς γέενναν) and states that the text had "before God" where canonical Luke has "before the messengers of God". Both are printed. NA27 cites Marcion for the omission of "the messengers of" in both 12:8 and 12:9.

Epiphanius, sch. 29: the text "did not have 'Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? And not one of them is forgotten before God'". In his refutation he presses Marcion with it: "nothing happens without God, even if you take away what is about the sparrows". 12:7 ("the hairs of your head are all numbered… you are of more value than many sparrows") depends on 12:6, and Tertullian, who goes straight from 12:5 to 12:8, does not cite it, though it would have suited his argument for the Creator's care. It is classed "unattested, probably absent".

Tertullian, Marc. 4.28.9–11. He sets Jesus' refusal to divide the inheritance ("Who made me a judge over you?") against Moses, who was rejected with the same words when he tried to make peace between two Hebrews (Exod 2:14), and quotes God's words to the rich man: "Fool, this night they will demand your soul; and what you have prepared, whose will it be?" 12:15, 12:17–18 and 12:21 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.29.1–5 recasts the passage rhetorically, but the lilies "neither weave nor spin" (D: "neither spin nor weave"), not "toil nor spin" as in canonical Luke, and he quotes "Seek the kingdom of God". Epiphanius, sch. 31–34 states that the text lacked "God clothes the grass" (12:28a), quotes 12:30b and 12:31 ("the kingdom of God"), and states that 12:32 read "the Father", not "your Father". The text printed therefore goes from Solomon not clothed like the lilies to "How much more you, you of little trust!" 12:25–26 and 12:29 are not cited and are printed in grey. 12:33–34 ("sell your possessions") form a paragraph that no witness cites and are not printed.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.29.6–11 reads the girded loins and burning lamps as the life of faith, asks from whose wedding the master returns, and says that the thief is the devil, while the son of the human comes as judge. He takes Peter's question to mean that the parable of the stewards is addressed to those "who would preside over the churches". Epiphanius, sch. 35 states that the master comes "in the evening watch", as in D and the Old Latin, not "in the second or third watch"; that reading is printed. Sch. 36 quotes 12:46. Tertullian reports that the Marcionites read "cut him in two" as mere separation (4.29.10); that is their reception, and the text has διχοτομήσει.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.29.12–16 quotes "Fire I came to throw upon the earth", "Do you think I came to bring peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but division", and the division of father and son, mother and daughter (Micah 7:6). He charges that "sword" is what is written and that Marcion changed it, but "sword" is Matthew's word (Matt 10:34); every Greek manuscript of Luke reads "division". He paraphrases 12:56 with "heaven and earth", the order of 𝔓45, 𝔓75 and D, which is printed. Epiphanius, sch. 37 quotes 12:58b. 12:50, 12:52 and 12:54–55 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Interpretation. In this text the Father knows what the learners need, gives them the kingdom, and the holy spirit teaches them what to say. Tertullian's argument through 4.28–4.29 is that the God who provides food and clothing and judges is one and the same. The text as attested does not separate a providing God from a judging one. It speaks of the Father who gives and of the one to be feared who can cast into Gehenna (12:5), and Tertullian identifies them. Whether the community behind the text read the two as one cannot be decided from the witnesses.
μυριάς, ten thousand, a countless number.

notes.term: Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἀπό, "keep yourselves away from"
notes.explanation: To watch oneself, be on guard against.
Sourdough, fermenting dough used to raise bread.
The acting of a part on stage (cf. ὑποκριτής, 6:42). "Hypocrisy" is the Greek word left untranslated.
One verb, καλύπτω, "cover", with two prefixes. "Revealed" is the second, and is uncovering.

notes.term: ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις, "in the inner rooms"
notes.explanation: The innermost room of a house, the storeroom.
Flat roofs, where people talked across to each other.
The body.
The reading of this text, βαλεῖν. Gehenna is the valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, a place of burning that became an image of judgement. "Hell" imports a later picture.
Literally "acknowledges in me", a Semitic idiom: to declare oneself for someone.
The reading of this text, "before God". Canonical Luke has "before the messengers of God".
ἀρνέομαι, as at 9:23.

notes.term: ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ, "it will be let go for him"
notes.explanation: ἀφίημι, passive.
As at 5:21.
Literally "beginnings": those first in rank.
μεριμνάω, to be anxious, to be pulled in different directions by worry. The same verb runs through 12:22–26.
To make one's defence in court.
As at 5:20.
One who divides an inheritance; a word from μερίζω, "divide" (12:13).
πλεονεξία is literally "having more", the desire for more than one's share. "Greed" gives the sense.

notes.term: ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν, "in having more than enough"
notes.explanation: To have a surplus, abundance.

notes.term: εὐφόρησεν ἡ χώρα, "the land bore well"
notes.explanation: The land itself produced richly.
καρπός, fruit, produce.
ἀγαθός, good, as at 6:45. In 12:19 the same word: "many good things".

notes.term: τῇ ψυχῇ μου· Ψυχή, "my soul: Soul"
notes.explanation: ψυχή, the living self. He speaks to himself.
To make merry, rejoice.
As at 11:40.
A plural with no named subject, "they demand back", as of a loan. The present tense: it is happening now.
From θησαυρός, treasure (6:45).
εἰς, "toward, into".
ψυχή, as at 9:24. Here "life" in the sense of the self that must eat.
To clothe oneself.
Unclean birds under the law.
To differ, to be worth more.
Height, or length of life. A cubit is a measure of length. The image can be read either way.
The superlative of μικρός.

notes.term: οὔτε νήθει οὔτε ὑφαίνει, "neither spin nor weave"
notes.explanation: The reading of this text, with D. Canonical Luke has "they neither toil nor spin".
To throw around oneself, to wrap.

notes.term: Πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι, "how much more you, you of little trust"
notes.explanation: This text does not have the first half of the verse ("if God so clothes the grass…"). The clause stands without its verb, and the English leaves it without one.
ὀλίγος, "little", and πίστις, "trust".

notes.term: μὴ μετεωρίζεσθε, "do not be held in suspense"
notes.explanation: Literally "do not be raised up in the air": to be unsettled, in suspense, anxious.

notes.term: τὰ ἔθνη τοῦ κόσμου, "the nations of the world"
notes.explanation: ἔθνη, the nations, the peoples other than Israel.
To have need of.
To be put to, added.
A small flock of sheep.
The reading of this text: "the Father", not "your Father".

notes.term: αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι, "your loins be girded"
notes.explanation: The long garment tucked up into the belt, for work or travel.
κύριος, the owner, the master of the house. "Lord" is kept here and in what follows, as everywhere in this text.

notes.term: ἀναλύσῃ ἐκ τῶν γάμων, "return from the wedding"
notes.explanation: To loosen, depart; γάμοι, wedding festivities.
As at 7:2.
To stay awake, keep watch.
Make them lie down at table.
διακονέω, to wait at table, as at 8:3.

notes.term: ἐν τῇ ἑσπερινῇ φυλακῇ, "in the evening watch"
notes.explanation: The reading of this text. Canonical Luke has "in the second or the third watch".

notes.term: ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης, "the master of the house"
notes.explanation: One word: the house-master. A different word from κύριος.
Walls of mud brick were broken into by digging.

notes.term: ᾗ ὥρᾳ οὐ δοκεῖτε, "at an hour you do not think"
notes.explanation: δοκέω, think, suppose.
Twice in one verse: the narrator's "the lord" (Jesus) and the lord of the parable. The Greek uses the same word.
πιστός, trustworthy; οἰκονόμος, manager of a house.
Prudent, thoughtful.
θεραπεία, the word for healing, also means the body of servants who attend a master.
The ration of food.
To delay, linger.

notes.term: τοὺς παῖδας καὶ τὰς παιδίσκας, "the slave boys and the slave girls"
notes.explanation: παῖς and παιδίσκη, the young slaves of the house.
To become drunk.
Word for word "cut in two". Some read it as "cut him off", a figure of speech; the Greek says the harsh thing.
ἄπιστος, the opposite of πιστός (12:42).

notes.term: δαρήσεται πολλάς, "will be beaten with many blows"
notes.explanation: δέρω, to flay, to beat.
They deposited with him, gave into his keeping. The verb is plural, with no named subject.
To light, set on fire.

notes.term: τί θέλω εἰ, "what do I want, if"
notes.explanation: Word for word. Often read as a wish: "how I wish it were already kindled!" The Greek allows both.

notes.term: βάπτισμα… βαπτισθῆναι, "an immersion to be immersed in"
notes.explanation: βαπτίζω, to dip, plunge, immerse. Here an image of being overwhelmed, as by flood waters.
To be held together, pressed hard, gripped.
To bring to its end, accomplish.
Splitting apart.
The reading of this text, with the Byzantine manuscripts.
Literally "bride": the son's wife in the father's house.
Where the sun sets: over the sea.
The wind from the desert.
As at 6:42.

notes.term: τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς, "of the sky and of the earth"
notes.explanation: The reading of this text: the sky first.
To test, assess, examine.
καιρός, the right or decisive time, a season.
δίκαιος, as at 5:32.
The other party in a lawsuit.
Literally "give work".
To be set free from, to settle.
The reading of this text. παραδίδωμι, as at 9:44.
The officer who collected debts and fines.
The smallest copper coin.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 11
chapters.preamble:
Something in us has been held fast for eighteen years by what binds it. On the day set apart for rest, it is loosed.

What keeps the order of our worship is indignant. There are six days for work; healing should keep to them. But every one of us unties an ox on that day and leads it to water. Why not this?

The kingdom, meanwhile, starts very small: a seed thrown into our own garden that becomes a tree with birds in its branches, a little leaven hidden in a great mass of flour until all of it rises.

And there is a door. One day the master of the house gets up and shuts it, and some of us are left outside, knocking. We remind him that we ate and drank with him, and that he taught in our streets.

He does not know where we are from.

verses.english: And he was teaching in one of the assemblies on the sabbaths.
verses.greek: Ἦν δὲ διδάσκων ἐν μιᾷ τῶν συναγωγῶν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν.

verses.english: And look, a woman having a spirit of weakness for eighteen years, and she was bent together and unable to straighten up at all.
verses.greek: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ πνεῦμα ἔχουσα ἀσθενείας ἔτη δεκαοκτώ, καὶ ἦν συγκύπτουσα καὶ μὴ δυναμένη ἀνακύψαι εἰς τὸ παντελές.

verses.english: And seeing her, Jesus called to her and said to her, "Woman, you have been released from your weakness,"
verses.greek: ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὴν ὁ Ἰησοῦς προσεφώνησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Γύναι, ἀπολέλυσαι τῆς ἀσθενείας σου,

verses.english: and he laid his hands on her; and at once she was made straight, and she was giving glory to God.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτῇ τὰς χεῖρας· καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνωρθώθη, καὶ ἐδόξαζεν τὸν θεόν.

verses.english: But the ruler of the assembly, answering, indignant because Jesus had healed on the sabbath, was saying to the crowd, "There are six days on which one must work; so come on those and be healed, and not on the day of the sabbath."
verses.greek: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος, ἀγανακτῶν ὅτι τῷ σαββάτῳ ἐθεράπευσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ἔλεγεν τῷ ὄχλῳ ὅτι Ἓξ ἡμέραι εἰσὶν ἐν αἷς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι· ἐν αὐταῖς οὖν ἐρχόμενοι θεραπεύεσθε καὶ μὴ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου.

verses.english: But the lord answered him and said, "Play-actors! Does not each of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away to give it drink?
verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος καὶ εἶπεν· Ὑποκριταί, ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τῷ σαββάτῳ οὐ λύει τὸν βοῦν αὐτοῦ ἢ τὸν ὄνον ἀπὸ τῆς φάτνης καὶ ἀπαγαγὼν ποτίζει;

verses.english: And this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound, look, eighteen years, was it not necessary that she be loosed from this bond on the day of the sabbath?"
verses.greek: ταύτην δὲ θυγατέρα Ἀβραὰμ οὖσαν, ἣν ἔδησεν ὁ Σατανᾶς ἰδοὺ δέκα καὶ ὀκτὼ ἔτη, οὐκ ἔδει λυθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δεσμοῦ τούτου τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;

verses.english: And as he was saying these things, all who were opposed to him were put to shame, and the whole crowd was rejoicing at all the glorious things being done by him.
verses.greek: καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντος αὐτοῦ κατῃσχύνοντο πάντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι αὐτῷ, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἔχαιρεν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐνδόξοις τοῖς γινομένοις ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: So he was saying, "What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I liken it?
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν οὖν· Τίνι ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τίνι ὁμοιώσω αὐτήν;

verses.english: It is like a grain of mustard, which a person took and threw into his own garden; and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky settled in its branches."
verses.greek: ὁμοία ἐστὶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔβαλεν εἰς κῆπον ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ ηὔξησεν καὶ ἐγένετο εἰς δένδρον, καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατεσκήνωσεν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And again he said, "To what shall I liken the kingdom of God?
verses.greek: Καὶ πάλιν εἶπεν· Τίνι ὁμοιώσω τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ;

verses.english: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until the whole was leavened."
verses.greek: ὁμοία ἐστὶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ἐνέκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.

verses.english: And someone said to him, "Lord, are those being saved few?" And he said to them,
verses.greek: εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ ὀλίγοι οἱ σῳζόμενοι; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς·

verses.english: "Struggle to go in through the narrow door, because many, I tell you, will seek to go in and will not be strong enough.
verses.greek: Ἀγωνίζεσθε εἰσελθεῖν διὰ τῆς στενῆς θύρας, ὅτι πολλοί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ζητήσουσιν εἰσελθεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἰσχύσουσιν,

verses.english: From the time the master of the house has got up and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, 'Lord, open to us,' then answering he will say to you, 'I do not know you, where you are from.'
verses.greek: ἀφ’ οὗ ἂν ἐγερθῇ ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης καὶ ἀποκλείσῃ τὴν θύραν, καὶ ἄρξησθε ἔξω ἑστάναι καὶ κρούειν τὴν θύραν λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν· καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ἐρεῖ ὑμῖν· Οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς πόθεν ἐστέ.

verses.english: Then you will begin to say, 'We ate and drank before you, and you taught in our streets.'
verses.greek: τότε ἄρξεσθε λέγειν· Ἐφάγομεν ἐνώπιόν σου καὶ ἐπίομεν, καὶ ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις ἡμῶν ἐδίδαξας·

verses.english: And he will say, speaking to you, 'I do not know you, where you are from. Stand away from me, all you workers of injustice.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἐρεῖ λέγων ὑμῖν· Οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς πόθεν ἐστέ· ἀπόστητε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, πάντες ἐργάται ἀδικίας.

verses.english: There, there will be the weeping and the grinding of the teeth, when you see all the just in the kingdom of God, but yourselves held outside."
verses.greek: ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων, ὅταν ὄψησθε πάντας τοὺς δικαίους ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὑμᾶς δὲ κρατουμένους ἔξω.

notes.explanation: Epiphanius, sch. 38: the text "was cut off" from "some came and told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices", through the eighteen killed by the tower in Siloam and "unless you repent", to the parable of the fig tree and the vinedresser's "I will dig and put on manure; and if it does not bear fruit, cut it down". Tertullian goes from 12:59 to the sabbath healing (13:14). The charge of cutting is Epiphanius'. What it reports as content is that the passage was not in the text.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.30.1: asked again about a healing on the sabbath, Christ answers "Does not each of you on the sabbaths untie his donkey or ox from the manger and lead it to drink?" Tertullian concludes that he "confirmed the law, not dissolved it", since the law permits work done to save a life. Epiphanius, sch. 39 quotes 13:16: "this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound". 13:10–13 and 13:17 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.30.1–3 quotes the mustard seed "which a man took and sowed in his garden" and asks whose garden the world is. Of the leaven he says mockingly that the kingdom of the other God might be compared to leaven because the Creator prefers unleavened bread. 13:18 is not cited and is printed in grey. 13:22, a travel notice, forms a paragraph that no witness cites and is not printed.

notes.term: The shut door and "all the just" (13:23–28)
notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.30.4–6: the master of the house rises and shuts the door; to those knocking he answers "I do not know where you are from"; to those who say they ate and drank before him and that he taught in their streets, "Depart from me, all workers of iniquity. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth", "when they see the just entering the kingdom of God and themselves held outside". Epiphanius, sch. 40 confirms the wording: the text had "all the just" where canonical Luke has "Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets", and "held" (κρατουμένους) outside. 13:23–24 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Epiphanius, sch. 41 names every saying of 13:29–35 as absent: people coming from east and west to recline in the kingdom, "the last will be first", the Pharisees' warning about Herod, the answer to "that fox", "no prophet can perish outside Jerusalem", and the lament "Jerusalem, Jerusalem" with "you will not see me until you say, Blessed…". Tertullian goes from 13:28 to 14:12.

Interpretation. In the attested text those seen in the kingdom are "all the just", not the patriarchs and prophets by name, while the woman healed on the sabbath is still "a daughter of Abraham" (13:16). The text therefore does not cut the tie to Abraham. It describes the kingdom by justness, not by descent. The leader of the Jerusalem community was remembered as James "the Just" (Gospel of Thomas 12; Carriers of Living Water §3.1). Whether "the just" in this saying reflects that usage cannot be shown from the witnesses. The readings themselves are attested by two witnesses; why canonical Luke has the patriarchs instead (as Matt 8:11 does) they do not say.
Plural, as at 4:31.

notes.term: πνεῦμα ἔχουσα ἀσθενείας, "having a spirit of weakness"
notes.explanation: Word for word. In 13:16 the text names its cause: Satan bound her.
Bent double, stooped.

notes.term: ἀνακύψαι εἰς τὸ παντελές, "straighten up at all"
notes.explanation: To raise oneself up. εἰς τὸ παντελές can mean "at all" or "fully".
A plain, respectful address, as the Greek has it.
ἀπολύω, to set free, as at 6:37. A perfect passive: released, and remaining free.
A passive: she was set upright.

notes.term: ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος, "the ruler of the assembly"
notes.explanation: As at 8:49.
Angry, vexed.
Necessity, as at 4:43. In 13:16 Jesus answers with the same word, ἔδει.
As at 7:13.
Plural, as at 12:56.
λύω, to untie, loose. 13:16 uses the same verb of the woman.
To water.
δέω, to bind. As at 11:18, the Hebrew word "adversary" left untranslated.
Here "ten and eight", as the Greek has it; in 13:11 it is the single word δεκαοκτώ.
The same word as in 13:14: what must be done.

notes.term: λυθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δεσμοῦ, "be loosed from this bond"
notes.explanation: λύω, as in 13:15.
Literally "lying against", adversaries.
From δόξα, glory.
A single seed of mustard.
βάλλω, to throw, cast, sow by casting.
To pitch a tent, take up a dwelling, as at 9:58.
To hide in.

notes.term: ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία, "three measures of flour"
notes.explanation: σάτον, a Hebrew measure (se'ah). Three of them make a very large amount of dough.
A present participle: those who are being saved.
To contend, as in an athletic contest.

notes.term: οὐκ ἰσχύσουσιν, "will not be strong enough"
notes.explanation: ἰσχύω, to have strength.

notes.term: ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης, "the master of the house"
notes.explanation: As at 12:39.
ἐγείρω.

notes.term: Οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς πόθεν ἐστέ, "I do not know you, where you are from"
notes.explanation: The Greek puts "you" first, then "where you are from".

notes.term: ἀπόστητε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ, "stand away from me"
notes.explanation: ἀφίστημι, to stand off, withdraw.
ἀδικία, wrong, injustice, the opposite of what is δίκαιος.

notes.term: ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων, "the weeping and the grinding of the teeth"
notes.explanation: With the article: "the weeping and the grinding", as of something known.
The reading of this text. Canonical Luke has "Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets".
The reading of this text. Canonical Luke has "thrown out".

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 12
chapters.preamble:
There is a kind of hospitality that is really an exchange. We invite whatever in us can invite us back, and the meal is paid off before it is eaten.

A great dinner is made ready, and the call goes out: come, it is ready now. Everything that was invited has something else to see to first. A field has just been bought and must be looked at. Five yoke of oxen must be tried out. A marriage has been made, and that settles it.

So the call goes out again, into the streets and lanes, to what is poor in us, crippled, blind and lame, the parts we never thought to ask. They come. There is still room.

Then further, to the roads and the hedges, the edges of the edges, until the house is full.

None of those first invited will taste the dinner.

verses.english: And he was saying also to the one who had invited him, "When you make a midday meal or a dinner, do not call your friends nor your brothers nor your relatives nor rich neighbours, so that they too do not invite you in return and it becomes a repayment to you.
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τῷ κεκληκότι αὐτόν· Ὅταν ποιῇς ἄριστον ἢ δεῖπνον, μὴ φώνει τοὺς φίλους σου μηδὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου μηδὲ τοὺς συγγενεῖς σου μηδὲ γείτονας πλουσίους, μήποτε καὶ αὐτοὶ ἀντικαλέσωσίν σε καὶ γένηται ἀνταπόδομά σοι.

verses.english: But when you make a reception, call the destitute, the crippled, the lame, the blind;
verses.greek: ἀλλ’ ὅταν δοχὴν ποιῇς, κάλει πτωχούς, ἀναπείρους, χωλούς, τυφλούς·

verses.english: and you will be fortunate, because they have nothing to repay you with; for it will be repaid to you at the rising of the just."
verses.greek: καὶ μακάριος ἔσῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνταποδοῦναί σοι, ἀνταποδοθήσεται γάρ σοι ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῶν δικαίων.

verses.english: And one of those reclining at table with him, hearing these things, said to him, "Fortunate is whoever will eat bread in the kingdom of God."
verses.greek: Ἀκούσας δέ τις τῶν συνανακειμένων ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακάριος ὅστις φάγεται ἄρτον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: But he said to him, "A certain person was making a great dinner, and he invited many,
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπός τις ἐποίει δεῖπνον μέγα, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν πολλούς,

verses.english: and he sent his slave at the hour of the dinner to say to those who had been invited, 'Come, because it is already ready.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ δείπνου εἰπεῖν τοῖς κεκλημένοις· Ἔρχεσθε, ὅτι ἤδη ἕτοιμά ἐστιν.

verses.english: And they all alike began to excuse themselves. The first said to him, 'I have bought a field, and I have need to go out and see it; I ask you, have me excused.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀπὸ μιᾶς πάντες παραιτεῖσθαι. ὁ πρῶτος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀγρὸν ἠγόρασα καὶ ἔχω ἀνάγκην ἐξελθὼν ἰδεῖν αὐτόν· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.

verses.english: And another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am journeying to test them; I ask you, have me excused.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν· Ζεύγη βοῶν ἠγόρασα πέντε καὶ πορεύομαι δοκιμάσαι αὐτά· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.

verses.english: And another said, 'I have married a wife, and because of this I cannot come.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν· Γυναῖκα ἔγημα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οὐ δύναμαι ἐλθεῖν.

verses.english: And the slave arrived and reported these things to his lord. Then the master of the house, angered, said to his slave, 'Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the destitute and crippled and blind and lame.'
verses.greek: καὶ παραγενόμενος ὁ δοῦλος ἀπήγγειλεν τῷ κυρίῳ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα. τότε ὀργισθεὶς ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης εἶπεν τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ· Ἔξελθε ταχέως εἰς τὰς πλατείας καὶ ῥύμας τῆς πόλεως, καὶ τοὺς πτωχοὺς καὶ ἀναπείρους καὶ τυφλοὺς καὶ χωλοὺς εἰσάγαγε ὧδε.

verses.english: And the slave said, 'Lord, what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.'
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ δοῦλος· Κύριε, γέγονεν ὃ ἐπέταξας, καὶ ἔτι τόπος ἐστίν.

verses.english: And the lord said to the slave, 'Go out into the roads and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled.
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος πρὸς τὸν δοῦλον· Ἔξελθε εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς καὶ φραγμοὺς καὶ ἀνάγκασον εἰσελθεῖν, ἵνα γεμισθῇ μου ὁ οἶκος·

verses.english: For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste my dinner.'"
verses.greek: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων τῶν κεκλημένων γεύσεταί μου τοῦ δείπνου.

notes.explanation: The healing of a man with dropsy on the sabbath and the advice to take the lowest place at table are not cited by Tertullian or Epiphanius. They form two NA27 paragraphs with no attested verse, and their absence is undetermined. Tertullian had just argued the sabbath question at 13:15 (4.30.1), and a second sabbath healing would have added nothing new to his case.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.31.1 sets the command to invite those who cannot repay beside Isaiah 58:7 ("break your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house"). He notes that Christ promises the repayment "in the resurrection". 14:13 is not cited and is printed in grey.

Tertullian, Marc. 4.31.1–8 follows the parable step by step: a man made a dinner and invited many, sent to those invited, they excused themselves ("I have bought a field, I have bought oxen, I have married a wife"), the householder was moved and sent into the streets and lanes, then, with room to spare, into the roads and hedges. He remarks that Marcion denies that his God is ever moved to anger. He reads the excuses as Israel refusing the prophets (Jer 7:23–26) and the second gathering as the call of the nations (Deut 32:20–21). 14:15 is not cited; it is printed in grey because the parable answers it.

Hating father and mother, carrying one's cross, counting the cost of a tower or a war, and the salt that loses its taste. No witness cites any of these verses as part of the text, and they are not printed. The previous version printed 14:26 and 14:33.

Interpretation. In the attested text the host's duty is to invite those who cannot repay, and the parable ends with the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame brought in, and then strangers from the roads. Tertullian reads this as the Creator's own pattern (Isaiah 58). The same preference for the destitute (πτωχοί) over the rich appears in the Epistle of James (Jas 2:1–7, the rich man and the poor man in the assembly).

notes.term: τῷ κεκληκότι αὐτόν, "the one who had invited him"
notes.explanation: καλέω, to call, invite. The same verb runs through the passage: "call" (14:12–13), "invited" (14:16–17, 14:24).

notes.term: ἄριστον ἢ δεῖπνον, "a midday meal or a dinner"
notes.explanation: ἄριστον, as at 11:37; δεῖπνον, the main meal of the day, in the evening.
φωνέω, to call out, invite. It is a different verb from καλέω.
What is given back in return.
As at 5:29.
As at 6:20.
Maimed, disabled.
μακάριος, as at 6:20.

notes.term: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῶν δικαίων, "at the rising of the just"
notes.explanation: ἀνάστασις, a standing up, rising. "Resurrection" is the Latin technical term (resurrectio) for the same word.

notes.term: Μακάριος ὅστις φάγεται ἄρτον, "fortunate is whoever will eat bread"
notes.explanation: ἄρτος, bread, a loaf.
καλέω, as in 14:12.
As at 7:2.
Plural in the Greek: "things are ready".
Literally "from one": with one accord, all at once.

notes.term: παραιτεῖσθαι… ἔχε με παρῃτημένον, "excuse themselves… have me excused"
notes.explanation: παραιτέομαι, to beg off, decline.
Literally "I have necessity": I must.
As at 12:56.

notes.term: Γυναῖκα ἔγημα, "I have married a wife"
notes.explanation: γυνή is both "woman" and "wife".

notes.term: τῷ κυρίῳ αὐτοῦ… ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης, "his lord… the master of the house"
notes.explanation: Two words for the same man: κύριος, lord, owner; οἰκοδεσπότης, master of the house (12:39).
Made angry.
The broad streets and the narrow alleys.
The slave's address to his owner.
ἐπιτάσσω, as at 4:36.
Fences, hedges along the fields.
To force, constrain. The Greek says "compel".
Filled full.
ἀνήρ, males.
γεύομαι, to taste, as at 9:27.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 13
chapters.preamble:
Most of what we are has never strayed: ninety-nine parts that stay where they are put and need nothing changed. One has gone missing, and that is where the whole attention goes.

The ninety-nine are left in the wilderness. The lost one is followed until it is found, and then it is not driven home but carried, on the shoulders, with joy. Everyone nearby is called in to rejoice.

The second time the loss is smaller and closer. A single coin out of ten has rolled away somewhere inside the house. A lamp is lit. The whole house is swept and searched, every corner, until it turns up.

Neither of them is scolded. Neither is asked where it has been.

There is more joy over one that turns than over all that never needed to.

verses.english: And all the tax collectors and the sinners were drawing near to him to hear him.
verses.greek: Ἦσαν δὲ αὐτῷ ἐγγίζοντες πάντες οἱ τελῶναι καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And both the Pharisees and the scribes were grumbling, saying, "This man receives sinners and eats with them."
verses.greek: καὶ διεγόγγυζον οἵ τε Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ἁμαρτωλοὺς προσδέχεται καὶ συνεσθίει αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: And he spoke this parable to them, saying,
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγων·

verses.english: "What person among you, having a hundred sheep and having lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the desert and journey after the one that is lost until he finds it?
verses.greek: Τίς ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ὑμῶν ἔχων ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ ἀπολέσας ἐξ αὐτῶν ἓν οὐ καταλείπει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ καὶ πορεύεται ἐπὶ τὸ ἀπολωλὸς ἕως εὕρῃ αὐτό;

verses.english: And having found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing,
verses.greek: καὶ εὑρὼν ἐπιτίθησιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους αὐτοῦ χαίρων,

verses.english: and coming into the house, he calls together the friends and the neighbours, saying to them, 'Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost.'
verses.greek: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον συγκαλεῖ τοὺς φίλους καὶ τοὺς γείτονας, λέγων αὐτοῖς· Συγχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὸ πρόβατόν μου τὸ ἀπολωλός.

verses.english: I tell you that in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who changes his mind, rather than over ninety-nine just people who have no need of a change of mind.
verses.greek: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως χαρὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἔσται ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι ἢ ἐπὶ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα δικαίοις οἵτινες οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν μετανοίας.

verses.english: Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and seek carefully until she finds it?
verses.greek: Ἢ τίς γυνὴ δραχμὰς ἔχουσα δέκα, ἐὰν ἀπολέσῃ δραχμὴν μίαν, οὐχὶ ἅπτει λύχνον καὶ σαροῖ τὴν οἰκίαν καὶ ζητεῖ ἐπιμελῶς ἕως οὗ εὕρῃ;

verses.english: And having found it, she calls together the women friends and neighbours, saying, 'Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma that I lost.'
verses.greek: καὶ εὑροῦσα συγκαλεῖ τὰς φίλας καὶ γείτονας λέγουσα· Συγχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα.

verses.english: In the same way, I tell you, there comes to be joy before the messengers of God over one sinner who changes his mind."
verses.greek: οὕτως, λέγω ὑμῖν, γίνεται χαρὰ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.32.1–2: "Who looks for the lost sheep and the lost coin? Surely the one who lost them. And who lost them? The one who had them. And who had them? The one whose they were." Since man belongs to the Creator, he concludes, the joy over the sinner's repentance is the Creator's, "who said long ago that he prefers the repentance of a sinner to his death" (Ezek 18:23). 15:1–2 are not cited. They are printed in grey because the parables answer them.

Epiphanius, sch. 42: "again he cut out the whole parable of the two sons, the one who took his share of the property and spent it wastefully, and the other". Tertullian, after the coin, goes to the two masters (16:13). The parable would have served him: its father receives back a son who left his house, the Creator's own image of repentance. Two witnesses agree that it was not there. "Cut out" is Epiphanius' charge; the content of his statement is that the parable was absent.

Interpretation. Tertullian's argument, "no one looks for what he never had", is aimed at the Marcionite claim that a stranger God redeems humans who were not his. The attested parables themselves say only that the one who lost the sheep or coin is the one who looks for it and rejoices. The Prodigal Son, which carries the theme of return most fully in canonical Luke, is absent here; in this text the theme rests on the two short parables alone.
The imperfect with a participle: they kept coming near.
γογγύζω as at 5:30, strengthened with δια-.
To receive, welcome, admit.
One word: "eats together with".

notes.term: ἀπολέσας… τὸ ἀπολωλός, "having lost… the one that is lost"
notes.explanation: ἀπόλλυμι, the verb of "destroy" (4:34) and "perish" (8:24). The same verb is "lose" here.
As at 4:42.
The road verb, as at 4:30.
The present tense, kept.
καλέω with συν-, as in 14:12.
μετανοέω, to change one's mind, as at 5:32.
ἤ, "than": the Greek has no word for "more".
δίκαιος, as at 5:32.
A silver coin, a day's wage.
To sweep clean.
With care.
The Greek is feminine.

notes.term: ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ, "before the messengers of God"
notes.explanation: ἄγγελος, messenger, as at 9:26.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 14
chapters.preamble:
What manages our goods for us is told to hand over the accounts. Before it goes, it does something unexpected: it calls in everything that owes, and writes the debts down. Even what is not truly ours can be used to make friends.

No one can serve two masters. Part of us, fond of silver, hears that and turns up its nose.

Then two lives, side by side. One is dressed in purple and feasts every day. The other lies at its gate, covered in sores, longing for what falls from the table, and the dogs come and lick him. Both die. Now they see one another across a chasm that no one can cross.

The one in the flame asks for a messenger from the dead, to warn the five still at home. The answer is that they already have every warning they need.

Someone rising from the dead will not move a soul that does not listen.

verses.english: And he was saying also to the learners, "There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and this one was accused to him of scattering his possessions.
verses.greek: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς· Ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν πλούσιος ὃς εἶχεν οἰκονόμον, καὶ οὗτος διεβλήθη αὐτῷ ὡς διασκορπίζων τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And calling him, he said to him, 'What is this I hear about you? Give back the account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward.'
verses.greek: καὶ φωνήσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί τοῦτο ἀκούω περὶ σοῦ; ἀπόδος τὸν λόγον τῆς οἰκονομίας σου, οὐ γὰρ δύνῃ ἔτι οἰκονομεῖν.

verses.english: And the steward said within himself, 'What shall I do, since my lord is taking the stewardship away from me? To dig I am not strong enough; to beg I am ashamed.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὁ οἰκονόμος· Τί ποιήσω ὅτι ὁ κύριός μου ἀφαιρεῖται τὴν οἰκονομίαν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ; σκάπτειν οὐκ ἰσχύω, ἐπαιτεῖν αἰσχύνομαι·

verses.english: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship they will receive me into their own houses.'
verses.greek: ἔγνων τί ποιήσω, ἵνα ὅταν μετασταθῶ ἐκ τῆς οἰκονομίας δέξωνταί με εἰς τοὺς οἴκους ἑαυτῶν.

verses.english: And calling to him each one of his lord's debtors, he was saying to the first, 'How much do you owe my lord?'
verses.greek: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα ἕκαστον τῶν χρεοφειλετῶν τοῦ κυρίου ἑαυτοῦ ἔλεγεν τῷ πρώτῳ· Πόσον ὀφείλεις τῷ κυρίῳ μου;

verses.english: And he said, 'A hundred baths of olive oil.' And he said to him, 'Take your writings, and sitting down quickly, write fifty.'
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἑκατὸν βάτους ἐλαίου· ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ καθίσας ταχέως γράψον πεντήκοντα.

verses.english: Then he said to another, 'And you, how much do you owe?' And he said, 'A hundred kors of wheat.' He says to him, 'Take your writings, and write eighty.'
verses.greek: ἔπειτα ἑτέρῳ εἶπεν· Σὺ δὲ πόσον ὀφείλεις; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἑκατὸν κόρους σίτου· λέγει αὐτῷ· Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ γράψον ὀγδοήκοντα.

verses.english: And the lord praised the steward of injustice, because he had acted sensibly; for the sons of this age are more sensible than the sons of the light toward their own generation.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπῄνεσεν ὁ κύριος τὸν οἰκονόμον τῆς ἀδικίας ὅτι φρονίμως ἐποίησεν· ὅτι οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου φρονιμώτεροι ὑπὲρ τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ φωτὸς εἰς τὴν γενεὰν τὴν ἑαυτῶν εἰσιν.

verses.english: And I say to you, make friends for yourselves out of the Mammon of injustice, so that when it gives out they may receive you into the tents of the age.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, ἑαυτοῖς ποιήσατε φίλους ἐκ τοῦ μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας, ἵνα ὅταν ἐκλίπῃ δέξωνται ὑμᾶς εἰς τὰς αἰωνίους σκηνάς.

verses.english: The one who is trustworthy in the least is trustworthy also in much, and the one who is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
verses.greek: Ὁ πιστὸς ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ καὶ ἐν πολλῷ πιστός ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ ἄδικος καὶ ἐν πολλῷ ἄδικός ἐστιν.

verses.english: If then you have not been trustworthy with the unjust Mammon, who will entrust the true to you?
verses.greek: εἰ οὖν ἐν τῷ ἀδίκῳ μαμωνᾷ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ἀληθινὸν τίς ὑμῖν πιστεύσει;

verses.english: And if you have not been trustworthy with what belongs to another, who will give you what is mine?
verses.greek: καὶ εἰ ἐν τῷ ἀλλοτρίῳ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ἐμὸν τίς ὑμῖν δώσει;

verses.english: No household slave can be a slave to two lords; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to one and despise the other. You cannot be a slave to God and to Mammon."
verses.greek: οὐδεὶς οἰκέτης δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.

verses.english: And the Pharisees, being lovers of silver, were hearing all these things, and they were turning up their noses at him.
verses.greek: Ἤκουον δὲ ταῦτα πάντα οἱ Φαρισαῖοι φιλάργυροι ὑπάρχοντες, καὶ ἐξεμυκτήριζον αὐτόν.

verses.english: And he said to them, "You are the ones who declare yourselves just before the humans, but God knows your hearts; because what is high among humans is an abomination before God.
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ δικαιοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁ δὲ θεὸς γινώσκει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν· ὅτι τὸ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὑψηλὸν βδέλυγμα ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: The law and the prophets were until John; from then the kingdom of God is announced as good news, and everyone forces his way into it.
verses.greek: Ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται μέχρι Ἰωάννου· ἀπὸ τότε ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγελίζεται καὶ πᾶς εἰς αὐτὴν βιάζεται.

verses.english: But it is easier for the sky and the earth to pass away than for one stroke of a letter of my words to fall.
verses.greek: Εὐκοπώτερον δέ ἐστιν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν παρελθεῖν ἢ τῶν λόγων μου μίαν κεραίαν πεσεῖν.

verses.english: Everyone who releases his wife and marries another commits adultery, and the one who marries a woman released from a husband commits adultery.
verses.greek: Πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμῶν ἑτέραν μοιχεύει, καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς γαμῶν μοιχεύει.

verses.english: There was a certain rich man, and he dressed in purple and fine linen, making merry every day splendidly.
verses.greek: Ἄνθρωπος δέ τις ἦν πλούσιος, καὶ ἐνεδιδύσκετο πορφύραν καὶ βύσσον εὐφραινόμενος καθ’ ἡμέραν λαμπρῶς.

verses.english: And a certain destitute man, named Lazarus, had been thrown down at his gateway, covered with sores,
verses.greek: πτωχὸς δέ τις ὀνόματι Λάζαρος ἐβέβλητο πρὸς τὸν πυλῶνα αὐτοῦ εἱλκωμένος

verses.english: and longing to be fed from what fell from the rich man's table; but even the dogs would come and lick his sores.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπιθυμῶν χορτασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τοῦ πλουσίου· ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ κύνες ἐρχόμενοι ἐπέλειχον τὰ ἕλκη αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And it happened that the destitute man died and was carried away by the messengers into the bosom of Abraham. And the rich man also died and was buried.
