verses.english: And you will say to the master of the house, 'The teacher says to you: Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my learners?'
verses.greek: καὶ ἐρεῖτε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ τῆς οἰκίας· Λέγει σοι ὁ διδάσκαλος· Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμα ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;

verses.english: And that one will show you a large upper room, spread out; make ready there."
verses.greek: κἀκεῖνος ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον· ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε.

verses.english: And going away, they found it just as he had told them, and they made ready the Passover.
verses.greek: ἀπελθόντες δὲ εὗρον καθὼς εἰρήκει αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.

verses.english: And when the hour came, he reclined at table, and the emissaries with him.
verses.greek: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡ ὥρα, ἀνέπεσεν καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι σὺν αὐτῷ.

verses.english: And he said to them, "With longing I have longed to eat this Passover with you before I suffer."
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπεθύμησα τοῦτο τὸ πάσχα φαγεῖν μεθ’ ὑμῶν πρὸ τοῦ με παθεῖν·

verses.english: And receiving a cup, having given thanks, he said, "Take this and divide it among yourselves;
verses.greek: καὶ δεξάμενος ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας εἶπεν· Λάβετε τοῦτο καὶ διαμερίσατε εἰς ἑαυτούς·

verses.english: for I tell you that from now on I will not drink at all of the produce of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."
verses.greek: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, ὅτι οὐ μὴ πίω ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως οὗ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἔλθῃ.

verses.english: And taking a loaf, having given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, "This is my body, which is given for you. Do this for my remembrance."
verses.greek: καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν διδόμενον· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.

verses.english: And the cup likewise after they had eaten, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
verses.greek: καὶ τὸ ποτήριον ὡσαύτως μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐν τῷ αἵματί μου, τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐκχυννόμενον.

verses.english: But look, the hand of the one who is handing me over is with me on the table;
verses.greek: πλὴν ἰδοὺ ἡ χεὶρ τοῦ παραδιδόντος με μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης·

verses.english: because the son of the human journeys according to what has been fixed; but woe to that human through whom he is handed over."
verses.greek: ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς μὲν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου κατὰ τὸ ὡρισμένον πορεύεται, πλὴν οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ δι’ οὗ παραδίδοται.

verses.english: And they began to question among themselves which of them it might be who was about to do this.
verses.greek: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς τὸ τίς ἄρα εἴη ἐξ αὐτῶν ὁ τοῦτο μέλλων πράσσειν.

verses.english: "Simon, Simon, look, Satan has asked to have you, to sift you like the wheat;
verses.greek: Σίμων Σίμων, ἰδοὺ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐξῃτήσατο ὑμᾶς τοῦ σινιάσαι ὡς τὸν σῖτον·

verses.english: but I have begged for you, that your trust may not give out; and you, when once you have turned back, make your brothers firm."
verses.greek: ἐγὼ δὲ ἐδεήθην περὶ σοῦ ἵνα μὴ ἐκλίπῃ ἡ πίστις σου· καὶ σύ ποτε ἐπιστρέψας στήρισον τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου.

verses.english: And he said to him, "Lord, with you I am ready to journey both into prison and into death."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μετὰ σοῦ ἕτοιμός εἰμι καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν καὶ εἰς θάνατον πορεύεσθαι.

verses.english: But he said, "I tell you, Peter, a rooster will not crow today until you have disowned three times that you know me."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Λέγω σοι, Πέτρε, οὐ φωνήσει σήμερον ἀλέκτωρ ἕως τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ εἰδέναι.

verses.english: And going out, he journeyed according to his custom to the Mountain of Olives; and the learners also followed him.
verses.greek: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη κατὰ τὸ ἔθος εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν· ἠκολούθησαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ μαθηταί.

verses.english: And when he was at the place, he said to them, "Pray that you do not come into testing."
verses.greek: γενόμενος δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦ τόπου εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Προσεύχεσθε μὴ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς πειρασμόν.

verses.english: And he himself was drawn away from them about a stone's throw, and kneeling down he was praying,
verses.greek: καὶ αὐτὸς ἀπεσπάσθη ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λίθου βολήν, καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύχετο

verses.english: saying, "Father, if you wish, take this cup away from me; yet not my will but yours be done."
verses.greek: λέγων· Πάτερ, εἰ βούλει παρένεγκε τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ· πλὴν μὴ τὸ θέλημά μου ἀλλὰ τὸ σὸν γινέσθω.

verses.english: And standing up from prayer, coming to the learners, he found them sleeping from grief,
verses.greek: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἀπὸ τῆς προσευχῆς ἐλθὼν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς εὗρεν κοιμωμένους αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς λύπης,

verses.english: and he said to them, "Why are you sleeping? Stand up and pray, so that you do not come into testing."
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί καθεύδετε; ἀναστάντες προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν.

verses.english: While he was still speaking, look, a crowd, and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was going ahead of them, and he drew near to Jesus to kiss him.
verses.greek: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ ὄχλος, καὶ ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα προήρχετο αὐτούς, καὶ ἤγγισεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ φιλῆσαι αὐτόν.

verses.english: But Jesus said to him, "Judas, with a kiss do you hand over the son of the human?"
verses.greek: Ἰησοῦς δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἰούδα, φιλήματι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδως;

verses.english: And the men who were holding him were mocking him, beating him,
verses.greek: Καὶ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ συνέχοντες αὐτὸν ἐνέπαιζον αὐτῷ δέροντες,

verses.english: and having covered him over, they were asking him, saying, "Prophesy: who is it who struck you?"
verses.greek: καὶ περικαλύψαντες αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτων λέγοντες· Προφήτευσον, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε;

verses.english: And they were saying many other things against him, blaspheming.
verses.greek: καὶ ἕτερα πολλὰ βλασφημοῦντες ἔλεγον εἰς αὐτόν.

verses.english: And when it became day, the council of elders of the people was gathered together, both high priests and scribes, and they led him away into their sanhedrin,
verses.greek: Καὶ ὡς ἐγένετο ἡμέρα, συνήχθη τὸ πρεσβυτέριον τοῦ λαοῦ, ἀρχιερεῖς τε καὶ γραμματεῖς, καὶ ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ συνέδριον αὐτῶν,

verses.english: saying, "If you are the Anointed One, tell us." But he said to them, "If I tell you, you will not trust at all;
verses.greek: λέγοντες· Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστός, εἰπὸν ἡμῖν. εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἐὰν ὑμῖν εἴπω οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε·

verses.english: and if I ask, you will not answer at all.
verses.greek: ἐὰν δὲ ἐρωτήσω, οὐ μὴ ἀποκριθῆτε.

verses.english: But from now on the son of the human will be seated at the right hand of the power of God."
verses.greek: ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν δὲ ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενος ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.english: And they all said, "Are you then the son of God?" And he said to them, "You say that I am."
verses.greek: εἶπαν δὲ πάντες· Σὺ οὖν εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ; ὁ δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἔφη· Ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι.

verses.english: And they said, "What further need do we have of testimony? For we ourselves have heard it from his mouth."
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Τί ἔτι ἔχομεν μαρτυρίας χρείαν; αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἠκούσαμεν ἀπὸ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ.

notes.explanation: Tertullian, Marc. 4.40.1–2: of all the Jewish feasts Jesus chose the day of the Passover; he could have been betrayed by a stranger and without a price, but was betrayed by one who ate bread with him, and for money, as the prophets said. In book 5 (5.6.7) Tertullian writes that "in my text" Satan entered Judas, against what holds "according to Marcion". The words "Satan entered into" (22:3) are therefore not printed, and the rest of the verse is put in the nominative. Epiphanius quotes 22:4 (sch. 60) with the order "how he might hand him over to them", which is printed.

Epiphanius quotes the sending of the learners to prepare the Passover (sch. 61) and Jesus reclining with "the twelve emissaries" (sch. 62). Both witnesses quote "With longing I have longed to eat this Passover with you before I suffer" (Tertullian 4.40.1; sch. 62). Epiphanius states that "I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God" (22:16) was not in the text (sch. 63). Tertullian (4.40.3–6) argues from the bread, "this is my body", and from the cup, "establishing the covenant sealed in his blood", that the body was real flesh. 22:17–18 are not cited and are printed in grey.

notes.term: The long text of the Supper (22:19–20)
notes.explanation: 22:19b–20 ("which is given for you… the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you") are absent from D and part of the Old Latin, and Westcott and Hort counted them among the Western non-interpolations. Tertullian's allusion to the cup and the covenant in Jesus' blood (4.40.4) shows that the text he read had at least 22:20 in some form, and his "then he should have handed over bread for us" points to "given for you". The second-century text attested here therefore stands with the long text, not with D (Roth, 259 n. 390). Both verses are printed as NA27 has them; the words the witness does not cite are noted.

22:16 is absent by Epiphanius' statement (sch. 63). 22:24–30, the dispute about greatness and the twelve thrones, form a paragraph with no attested verse; Epiphanius' "or he cut these out again" (elenchus 63) suggests that 22:30 was not in the text. 22:35–38, the purse, the bag and the two swords with "he was counted among the lawless" (Isa 53:12), are absent by Epiphanius' statement (sch. 64).

Epiphanius quotes "he was drawn away from them about a stone's throw, and kneeling down he was praying" (sch. 65) and argues from the kneeling that Jesus had a body. 22:43–44, the messenger from heaven and the sweat like drops of blood, are printed by NA27 in double brackets as not part of its text, and no witness cites them for this text; they are not printed. Judas draws near to kiss Jesus (sch. 66), and Tertullian notes that he was to be betrayed "with a kiss" (4.41.2). Epiphanius states that the cutting off of the slave's ear and its healing were not in the text (sch. 67); 22:49, which asks whether to strike with the sword, depends on the absent swords (22:38) and the absent blow and is not printed. 22:52–53 and Peter's denial (22:54–62) form paragraphs with no attested verse.

Epiphanius quotes the mockery, the beating and "Prophesy: who is it who struck you?" (sch. 68), as proof of a body that could be struck. Tertullian (4.41.3–5) follows the council: asked whether he is the Christ, Jesus answers "if I tell you, you will not trust at all"; "from now on the son of the human will be seated at the right hand of the power of God" (Dan 7:13; Ps 110:1); asked "are you then the son of God?", he answers "you say", which Tertullian takes as an affirmation.

Interpretation. Without "Satan entered into Judas", the betrayal in this text is the act of one of the twelve, done for money, and the "woe" of 22:22 falls on him; Tertullian (4.41.1) argues from that "woe" that the God of this Jesus judges. The meal is a Passover that Jesus has "longed with longing" to eat. In the attested text he gives the bread as his body and the cup as the covenant in his blood. Which canonical words go beyond what the witness cites ("do this in remembrance of me", "poured out for you") is recorded verse by verse; the verse-level evidence does not support reading this text as a fellowship meal without the cup of the covenant.

notes.term: ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἀζύμων, "the feast of the unleavened loaves"
notes.explanation: τὰ ἄζυμα, the unleavened breads.
Πάσχα is the Aramaic pasḥa, Hebrew pesach. It is used for both the feast and the lamb (22:7).
ἀναιρέω, to take away, kill.

notes.explanation: This text lacks "Satan entered into Judas". The sentence runs straight on into 22:4.
The form here differs from Ἰσκαριώθ at 6:16.
The commanders of the temple guard.

notes.explanation: The reading of this text. παραδίδωμι, as at 9:44: "betray" is one use; the word says "hand over".
Money, as at 9:3.
To agree, promise.
A fitting moment.

notes.term: ἔδει θύεσθαι τὸ πάσχα, "the Passover had to be sacrificed"
notes.explanation: Here τὸ πάσχα is the lamb. δεῖ, as at 4:43.
A clay jar.

notes.term: τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ, "the master of the house"
notes.explanation: As at 12:39.
A place to lodge.

notes.term: ἀνάγαιον… ἐστρωμένον, "an upper room… spread out"
notes.explanation: A room above the ground floor, furnished with couches.
As at 11:37.
As at 6:13.

notes.term: Ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπεθύμησα, "with longing I have longed"
notes.explanation: A Hebrew way of strengthening a verb by its own noun.

notes.term: πρὸ τοῦ με παθεῖν, "before I suffer"
notes.explanation: πάσχω, to suffer.
εὐχαριστέω, as at 10:21.

notes.term: τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου, "the produce of the vine"
notes.explanation: What the vine yields.
Without the article.
On your behalf.

notes.term: εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν, "for my remembrance"
notes.explanation: ἀνάμνησις, a calling to mind. The Greek has the possessive adjective, "my remembrance".
καινός, as at 5:36. διαθήκη is a covenant or a will.
The present tense: "which is being poured out". It is the verb of the young wine poured out (5:37).

notes.term: τοῦ παραδιδόντος με, "the one who is handing me over"
notes.explanation: A present participle.

notes.term: κατὰ τὸ ὡρισμένον, "according to what has been fixed"
notes.explanation: ὁρίζω, to mark out a boundary, determine.
The road verb, as at 4:30 and 9:51.
To discuss, dispute together.
As at 11:18.

notes.term: ἐξῃτήσατο ὑμᾶς, "has asked to have you"
notes.explanation: To ask for and obtain, to demand for oneself. "You" is plural: all of them.
To shake in a sieve.

notes.term: περὶ σοῦ… ἡ πίστις σου, "for you… your trust"
notes.explanation: Singular: Simon alone.
As at 16:9.
ἐπιστρέφω, as at 17:4.
στηρίζω, as at 9:51.
ἀρνέομαι, as at 9:23 and 12:9.

notes.explanation: As was his habit.
As at 11:4.
A passive: to be drawn off, to withdraw.
Literally "placing the knees".
As at 11:2.
βούλομαι, to will, decide, as at 10:22.
To carry past, remove.

notes.term: τὸ θέλημά μου… τὸ σόν, "my will… yours"
notes.explanation: θέλημα, what one wills, as at 12:47.
ἀνίστημι.
λύπη, sorrow, pain.
ἀνίστημι again.
To go before, lead.

notes.term: φιλήματι… παραδίδως, "with a kiss do you hand over"
notes.explanation: παραδίδωμι, as at 9:44.

notes.term: οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ συνέχοντες αὐτόν, "the men who were holding him"
notes.explanation: συνέχω, to hold fast, as at 8:45.
ἐμπαίζω, to make fun of, as of a child; δέρω, to beat, as at 12:47.
Blindfolded.

As at 5:21. The Greek uses the same word for insults against Jesus.

notes.term: τὸ πρεσβυτέριον τοῦ λαοῦ, "the council of elders of the people"
notes.explanation: The body of elders.

notes.explanation: πιστεύω, with the double negative.

notes.explanation: δύναμις, power, as at 6:19 and 9:1.

notes.term: Ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι, "you say that I am"
notes.explanation: The Greek allows "You say it, because I am", or "You are saying that I am". It is neither a plain yes nor a plain no.
Evidence of witnesses.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 21
chapters.preamble:
Every power in us that rules from outside now has truth in its hands. The prince of the edges has wanted to see it for a long time, hopes for a sign, and gets silence. The governor asks a third time what evil it has done: he has found no cause. But the voices are louder, and the voices win.

They ask instead for what was locked up for uprising and murder, and it is set free.

At the place of the skull, between two who did evil, truth is put to death. At midday the sun fails, darkness covers the whole land, and the curtain at the centre is torn down the middle. The last words are not a cry of defeat: into your hands.

Then one member of the very council that condemned it, who never agreed, comes forward and asks for the body. It is laid in rock where nothing has lain before.

The women who came from the edge watch where it is laid, make ready the spices, and rest.

verses.english: And the whole multitude of them, standing up, led him before Pilate.
verses.greek: Καὶ ἀναστὰν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος αὐτῶν ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Πιλᾶτον.

verses.english: And they began to accuse him, saying, "We found this man perverting our nation, and abolishing the law and the prophets, and forbidding to give tributes to Caesar, and turning away the women and the children, and saying that he himself is the Anointed One, a king."
verses.greek: ἤρξαντο δὲ κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Τοῦτον εὕραμεν διαστρέφοντα τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ καταλύοντα τὸν νόμον καὶ τοὺς προφήτας καὶ κωλύοντα φόρους Καίσαρι διδόναι καὶ ἀποστρέφοντα τὰς γυναῖκας καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ λέγοντα ἑαυτὸν χριστὸν βασιλέα εἶναι.

verses.english: And Pilate asked him, saying, "Are you the king of the Judeans?" And answering him, he said, "You say it."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔφη· Σὺ λέγεις.

verses.english: And Pilate said to the high priests and the crowds, "I find no cause in this man."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ὄχλους· Οὐδὲν εὑρίσκω αἴτιον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ.

verses.english: But they were insisting, saying, "He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee to here."
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἐπίσχυον λέγοντες ὅτι Ἀνασείει τὸν λαὸν διδάσκων καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἕως ὧδε.

verses.english: And Pilate, hearing it, asked whether the man was a Galilean;
verses.greek: Πιλᾶτος δὲ ἀκούσας ἐπηρώτησεν εἰ ὁ ἄνθρωπος Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν,

verses.english: and learning that he was from Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him up to Herod, who was himself also in Jerusalem in these days.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου ἐστὶν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν πρὸς Ἡρῴδην, ὄντα καὶ αὐτὸν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν ταύταις ταῖς ἡμέραις.

verses.english: And Herod, seeing Jesus, rejoiced greatly, for he had been wanting to see him for a long time, because of hearing about him, and he was hoping to see some sign done by him.
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐχάρη λίαν, ἦν γὰρ ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων θέλων ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ ἀκούειν περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἤλπιζέν τι σημεῖον ἰδεῖν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ γινόμενον.

verses.english: And he was questioning him with many words; but he answered him nothing.
verses.greek: ἐπηρώτα δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν λόγοις ἱκανοῖς· αὐτὸς δὲ οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτῷ.

verses.english: And the high priests and the scribes had been standing by, accusing him vehemently.
verses.greek: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς εὐτόνως κατηγοροῦντες αὐτοῦ.

verses.english: And Herod too, with his soldiers, treated him as nothing, and having mocked him, putting a bright garment around him, he sent him back to Pilate.
verses.greek: ἐξουθενήσας δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ Ἡρῴδης σὺν τοῖς στρατεύμασιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμπαίξας περιβαλὼν ἐσθῆτα λαμπρὰν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν τῷ Πιλάτῳ.

verses.english: And Herod and Pilate became friends with one another on that very day; for before they had been in enmity toward each other.
verses.greek: ἐγένοντο δὲ φίλοι ὅ τε Ἡρῴδης καὶ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ μετ’ ἀλλήλων· προϋπῆρχον γὰρ ἐν ἔχθρᾳ ὄντες πρὸς αὐτούς.

verses.english: And they cried out all together, saying, "Take this man away, and release Barabbas to us";
verses.greek: Ἀνέκραγον δὲ παμπληθεὶ λέγοντες· Αἶρε τοῦτον, ἀπόλυσον δὲ ἡμῖν τὸν Βαραββᾶν·

verses.english: who had been thrown into prison for a certain uprising that had happened in the city, and for murder.
verses.greek: ὅστις ἦν διὰ στάσιν τινὰ γενομένην ἐν τῇ πόλει καὶ φόνον βληθεὶς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ.

verses.english: And again Pilate called out to them, wanting to release Jesus.
verses.greek: πάλιν δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος προσεφώνησεν αὐτοῖς θέλων ἀπολῦσαι τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

verses.english: But they kept shouting, saying, "Crucify, crucify him!"
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἐπεφώνουν λέγοντες· Σταύρου σταύρου αὐτόν.

verses.english: And a third time he said to them, "Why, what evil has this man done? I have found no cause of death in him; so I will discipline him and release him."
verses.greek: ὁ δὲ τρίτον εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν οὗτος; οὐδὲν αἴτιον θανάτου εὗρον ἐν αὐτῷ· παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ἀπολύσω.

verses.english: But they were pressing with loud voices, asking for him to be crucified; and their voices were prevailing.
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἐπέκειντο φωναῖς μεγάλαις αἰτούμενοι αὐτὸν σταυρωθῆναι, καὶ κατίσχυον αἱ φωναὶ αὐτῶν.

verses.english: And Pilate decided that their request should be done;
verses.greek: καὶ Πιλᾶτος ἐπέκρινεν γενέσθαι τὸ αἴτημα αὐτῶν·

verses.english: and he released the one who had been thrown into prison for uprising and murder, whom they were asking for; but Jesus he handed over to their will.
verses.greek: ἀπέλυσεν δὲ τὸν διὰ στάσιν καὶ φόνον βεβλημένον εἰς φυλακὴν ὃν ᾐτοῦντο, τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν παρέδωκεν τῷ θελήματι αὐτῶν.

verses.english: And two others also, evil-doers, were being led with him to be done away with.
verses.greek: Ἤγοντο δὲ καὶ ἕτεροι κακοῦργοι δύο σὺν αὐτῷ ἀναιρεθῆναι.

verses.english: And when they came to the place called Skull, there they crucified him and the evil-doers, one on the right and one on the left.
verses.greek: καὶ ὅτε ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Κρανίον, ἐκεῖ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτὸν καὶ τοὺς κακούργους, ὃν μὲν ἐκ δεξιῶν ὃν δὲ ἐξ ἀριστερῶν.

verses.english: And it was already about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour,
verses.greek: Καὶ ἦν ἤδη ὡσεὶ ὥρα ἕκτη καὶ σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης

verses.english: the sun having failed; and the curtain of the sanctuary was torn in the middle.
verses.greek: τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλιπόντος, ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ μέσον.

verses.english: And calling out with a loud voice, Jesus said, "Father, into your hands I set my spirit." And having said this, he breathed out.
verses.greek: καὶ φωνήσας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Πάτερ, εἰς χεῖράς σου παρατίθεμαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου. τοῦτο δὲ εἰπὼν ἐξέπνευσεν.

verses.english: And look, a man named Joseph, being a member of the council, and a good and just man—
verses.greek: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι Ἰωσὴφ βουλευτὴς ὑπάρχων καὶ ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ δίκαιος—

verses.english: this one had not agreed with their counsel and action—from Arimathea, a city of the Judeans, who was waiting for the kingdom of God,
verses.greek: οὗτος οὐκ ἦν συγκατατεθειμένος τῇ βουλῇ καὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτῶν— ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας πόλεως τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὃς προσεδέχετο τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ,

verses.english: this one, coming to Pilate, asked for the body of Jesus,
verses.greek: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ,

verses.english: and taking it down, he wrapped it in linen, and laid him in a tomb cut in stone, where no one had yet been laid.
verses.greek: καὶ καθελὼν ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι, καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνήματι λαξευτῷ οὗ οὐκ ἦν οὐδεὶς οὔπω κείμενος.

verses.english: And it was the day of preparation, and the sabbath was dawning.
verses.greek: καὶ ἡμέρα ἦν παρασκευῆς, καὶ σάββατον ἐπέφωσκεν.

verses.english: And the women who had come with him out of Galilee, following after, looked at the tomb and how his body was laid,
verses.greek: κατακολουθήσασαι δὲ αἱ γυναῖκες, αἵτινες ἦσαν συνεληλυθυῖαι ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας αὐτῷ, ἐθεάσαντο τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ ὡς ἐτέθη τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ,

verses.english: and returning, they made ready spices and perfumed oils. And on the sabbath they rested, according to the commandment.
verses.greek: ὑποστρέψασαι δὲ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα καὶ μύρα. Καὶ τὸ μὲν σάββατον ἡσύχασαν κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν.

notes.explanation: Tertullian (4.42.1) has the council accuse Jesus of calling himself "Christ, a king", and Pilate ask "Are you the Christ?". Epiphanius reports two additions in the charges of 23:2: "and abolishing the law and the prophets" (sch. 69) and "and turning away the women and the children" (sch. 70). He answers the first from Matt 5:17 ("I came not to destroy the law and the prophets"), and says that the canonical text reads only "misleading the people". Old Latin manuscripts have the first addition at the same place, and c and e have the second at 23:5, so both readings were known outside Marcion's text. They are printed. 23:4–5 are not cited and are printed in grey.

Tertullian (4.42.2–4) reads the trial through Ps 2 and Isaiah: Herod receives Jesus "as a gift" from Pilate (Hos 10:6), is glad to see him and hears no word from him, as the lamb is silent before the shearer (Isa 53:7). Barabbas, "most guilty in life", is released as if good, and Christ, "most just", is demanded for death as a murderer. 23:13–16 form a paragraph that no witness cites and is not printed; NA27 has no 23:17.

Tertullian (4.42.4) attests the two criminals crucified with Jesus "so that he was counted among the lawless", and states that Marcion removed the dividing of his garments because of Ps 22:18; he answers that the whole psalm is Christ's garment. Epiphanius' scholion 71 mentions the dividing, but in a summary of the scene in Matthew's wording; Tertullian's statement is followed. Epiphanius states that "Today you will be with me in paradise" (23:43) was not in the text (sch. 72). Tertullian (4.42.5) attests the darkness at the sixth hour and the torn curtain, and (4.42.6) the loud cry to the Father and "having said this, he breathed out", from which he argues that what breathes out a spirit is flesh. "Father, forgive them" (23:34a) is not in the NA27 text and is not cited by either witness. Simon of Cyrene, the daughters of Jerusalem, the mockery at the cross, the criminals' exchange, the centurion and the onlookers (23:26–31, 35–42, 47–49) are in paragraphs that no witness cites.

Tertullian (4.42.7–8) argues from the burial: if the body were a phantom, nothing would have been asked of Pilate, taken down from the cross, wrapped in linen or laid in a new tomb; Joseph, "who had not consented to the crime", knew it was a body. Epiphanius quotes Joseph taking down the body, wrapping it in linen and laying it in a rock-cut tomb (sch. 74), and the women returning and resting on the Sabbath "according to the law" (sch. 75). Tertullian (4.43.1) attests the women who came to the tomb with spices.

Interpretation. In this text the charge that Jesus destroys the law and the prophets is made by his accusers before Pilate, beside the charges about tribute and about turning away women and children; the narrative does not endorse it. Irenaeus (Haer. 1.27.2, as cited by Roth, 337 n. 230) reports that Marcion taught that Christ abolished the law and the prophets; that belongs to the reception of the text, not to its wording. The reading itself is old and not confined to Marcion's text, since the Old Latin has it. Epiphanius' charge that Marcion added the words assumes that canonical Luke is the earlier text.
ἀνίστημι, used of the whole assembly rising.
To turn aside, twist, mislead.

notes.term: καταλύοντα τὸν νόμον καὶ τοὺς προφήτας, "abolishing the law and the prophets"
notes.explanation: Present in this text, and in the Old Latin. καταλύω, to loosen down, dissolve, abolish. Kept apart from ἀπόλλυμι, "destroy" (4:34).

notes.term: ἀποστρέφοντα τὰς γυναῖκας καὶ τὰ τέκνα, "turning away the women and the children"
notes.explanation: Present in this text, and in the Old Latin. ἀποστρέφω, to turn away, lead astray.
Plural, as at 20:22.

notes.term: χριστὸν βασιλέα, "the Anointed One, a king"
notes.explanation: Without articles in the Greek: "an anointed one, a king". The second word explains the first for a Roman.
As at 7:3.
As at 22:70: neither a plain yes nor a plain no.
A ground for a charge.
To grow stronger, press harder.
To shake up, incite.

notes.term: ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου, "from Herod's jurisdiction"
notes.explanation: ἐξουσία, here the area under Herod's authority.
To send up to a higher authority, or send back.

notes.term: ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων, "for a long time"
notes.explanation: As at 8:27.
With all their strength.
As at 18:9.
As at 22:63.
Shining, splendid clothing.
αἴρω, to lift, take away.
ἀπολύω, as at 6:37.
An Aramaic name, "son of the father".
A rebellion, revolt.
φόνος, as at 18:20.
The imperfect.
σταυρόω, to put on a stake or cross.
παιδεύω, to train a child, to punish, here to flog.
To lie upon, press hard.
To have the upper hand.
To give a judgement, decree.

notes.term: παρέδωκεν τῷ θελήματι αὐτῶν, "handed over to their will"
notes.explanation: παραδίδωμι, as at 9:44; θέλημα, as at 22:42.
Literally "those who do evil": criminals.
As at 22:2.
κρανίον, a skull: the Greek for the Aramaic Golgotha.

notes.term: ἐφ' ὅλην τὴν γῆν, "over the whole land"
notes.explanation: γῆ, land and earth, as at 5:24.

notes.term: ὥρα ἕκτη… ἐνάτης, "the sixth hour… the ninth"
notes.explanation: Counted from sunrise: about noon to three in the afternoon.

notes.term: τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλιπόντος, "the sun having failed"
notes.explanation: ἐκλείπω, to fail, give out, as at 16:9 and 22:32; used of an eclipse.

notes.term: τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ, "the curtain of the sanctuary"
notes.explanation: ναός, the inner sanctuary, as distinct from ἱερόν, the whole temple precinct.
Down the middle, as at 4:30.
To place beside, entrust, deposit. Ps 31:5.
To breathe one's last: the breath (πνεῦμα) goes out.
A councillor.
ἀγαθός, as at 6:45; δίκαιος, as at 5:32.
To vote with, consent to.

notes.term: τῇ βουλῇ καὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτῶν, "their counsel and action"
notes.explanation: βουλή, plan, decision; πρᾶξις, deed.
To wait for, expect, receive.
A linen cloth.

notes.term: ἐν μνήματι λαξευτῷ, "in a tomb cut in stone"
notes.explanation: Hewn out of rock.
The day before the sabbath.
Was beginning to shine: the sabbath began at sunset.
To follow behind closely.
As at 7:24.

notes.term: ἀρώματα καὶ μύρα, "spices and perfumed oils"
notes.explanation: μύρον, as at 7:37.
To be quiet, keep still.

chapters.title: Proto-Luke Chapter 22
chapters.preamble:
Very early, while it is still deep dawn, the part of us that stayed comes with spices for the dead and finds nothing to anoint. Two figures in flashing clothes ask the question that turns the whole book around: why seek the living among the dead?

What it reports sounds to the rest of us like idle talk.

Later, two of us are walking away, talking it over. Truth comes alongside and walks with them, and they do not know it. They describe it to its face by the old name, the one first heard in the assembly: a man, a prophet, and how they had hoped. They are slow of heart, and it is patient with them.

At the table it takes the bread, blesses it, breaks it and gives it, and their eyes are opened, and in the same moment it can no longer be seen.

Then, while we are still afraid it is only a spirit, it shows its hands and feet, and asks for something to eat.

verses.english: And on the first of the week, at deep dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had made ready.
verses.greek: τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ὄρθρου βαθέως ἐπὶ τὸ μνῆμα ἦλθον φέρουσαι ἃ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα.

verses.english: And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
verses.greek: εὗρον δὲ τὸν λίθον ἀποκεκυλισμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου,

verses.english: and going in, they did not find the body of the lord Jesus.
verses.greek: εἰσελθοῦσαι δὲ οὐχ εὗρον τὸ σῶμα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.

verses.english: And it happened, while they were at a loss about this, that look, two men stood by them in flashing clothing.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἀπορεῖσθαι αὐτὰς περὶ τούτου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο ἐπέστησαν αὐταῖς ἐν ἐσθῆτι ἀστραπτούσῃ.

verses.english: And as they became afraid and bowed their faces to the ground, they said to them, "Why do you seek the Living One among the dead?
verses.greek: ἐμφόβων δὲ γενομένων αὐτῶν καὶ κλινουσῶν τὰ πρόσωπα εἰς τὴν γῆν εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτάς· Τί ζητεῖτε τὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τῶν νεκρῶν;

verses.english: He has been raised. Remember all that he spoke to you while he was still in Galilee,
verses.greek: ἠγέρθη. μνήσθητε ὅσα ἐλάλησεν ὑμῖν ἔτι ὢν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ,

verses.english: saying of the son of the human that he must be handed over into the hands of sinful humans, and be crucified, and on the third day stand up."
verses.greek: λέγων τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὅτι δεῖ παραδοθῆναι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ σταυρωθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἀναστῆναι.

verses.english: And they remembered his sayings,
verses.greek: καὶ ἐμνήσθησαν τῶν ῥημάτων αὐτοῦ,

verses.english: and returning from the tomb, they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
verses.greek: καὶ ὑποστρέψασαι ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπήγγειλαν ταῦτα πάντα τοῖς ἕνδεκα καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς λοιποῖς.

verses.english: And they were Mary the Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of Jacob, and the other women with them. They were saying these things to the emissaries.
verses.greek: ἦσαν δὲ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ Μαρία καὶ Ἰωάννα καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ σὺν αὐταῖς· ἔλεγον πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ταῦτα.

verses.english: And these sayings appeared before them like idle talk, and they did not trust them.
verses.greek: καὶ ἐφάνησαν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λῆρος τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα, καὶ ἠπίστουν αὐταῖς.

verses.english: And look, two of them on that very day were journeying to a village sixty stadia distant from Jerusalem, whose name is Emmaus,
verses.greek: Καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἦσαν πορευόμενοι εἰς κώμην ἀπέχουσαν σταδίους ἑξήκοντα ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ᾗ ὄνομα Ἐμμαοῦς,

verses.english: and they were talking with one another about all these things that had happened.
verses.greek: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡμίλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους περὶ πάντων τῶν συμβεβηκότων τούτων.

verses.english: And it happened, while they were talking and questioning together, that Jesus himself drew near and was journeying with them;
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὁμιλεῖν αὐτοὺς καὶ συζητεῖν καὶ αὐτὸς Ἰησοῦς ἐγγίσας συνεπορεύετο αὐτοῖς,

verses.english: but their eyes were held fast, so that they did not recognise him.
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν ἐκρατοῦντο τοῦ μὴ ἐπιγνῶναι αὐτόν.

verses.english: And he said to them, "What are these words that you are exchanging with one another as you walk?" And they stood still, looking downcast.
verses.greek: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίνες οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι οὓς ἀντιβάλλετε πρὸς ἀλλήλους περιπατοῦντες; καὶ ἐστάθησαν σκυθρωποί.

verses.english: And answering, one named Cleopas said to him, "Are you the only one staying in Jerusalem who has not come to know the things that have happened in it in these days?"
verses.greek: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἷς ὀνόματι Κλεοπᾶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σὺ μόνος παροικεῖς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ οὐκ ἔγνως τὰ γενόμενα ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις;

verses.english: And he said to them, "What things?" And they said to him, "The things about Jesus the Nazarene, who was a man, a prophet, powerful in deed and word before God and all the people,
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ποῖα; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Τὰ περὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζαρηνοῦ, ὃς ἐγένετο ἀνὴρ προφήτης δυνατὸς ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ,

verses.english: and how our high priests and rulers handed him over to a sentence of death, and crucified him.
verses.greek: ὅπως τε παρέδωκαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν εἰς κρίμα θανάτου καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.

verses.english: But we thought that he is the one who was about to release Israel by ransom. But besides all these things, this is the third day since these things happened.
verses.greek: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐνομίζομεν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ μέλλων λυτροῦσθαι τὸν Ἰσραήλ· ἀλλά γε καὶ σὺν πᾶσιν τούτοις τρίτην ταύτην ἡμέραν ἄγει ἀφ’ οὗ ταῦτα ἐγένετο.

verses.english: But also some women from among us put us beside ourselves; having been at the tomb at dawn,
verses.greek: ἀλλὰ καὶ γυναῖκές τινες ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξέστησαν ἡμᾶς, γενόμεναι ὀρθριναὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον

verses.english: and not finding his body, they came, saying that they had even seen a vision of messengers, who say that he lives."
verses.greek: καὶ μὴ εὑροῦσαι τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἦλθον λέγουσαι καὶ ὀπτασίαν ἀγγέλων ἑωρακέναι, οἳ λέγουσιν αὐτὸν ζῆν.

verses.english: And he said to them, "O you without understanding and slow of heart to trust in all that he spoke to you!
verses.greek: καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὦ ἀνόητοι καὶ βραδεῖς τῇ καρδίᾳ τοῦ πιστεύειν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐλάλησεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς·

verses.english: Was it not necessary that the Anointed One suffer these things and go into his glory?"
verses.greek: οὐχὶ ταῦτα ἔδει παθεῖν τὸν χριστὸν καὶ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ;

verses.english: And they drew near to the village where they were journeying, and he made as if to journey farther.
verses.greek: Καὶ ἤγγισαν εἰς τὴν κώμην οὗ ἐπορεύοντο, καὶ αὐτὸς προσεποιήσατο πορρώτερον πορεύεσθαι.

verses.english: And they pressed him, saying, "Stay with us, because it is toward evening and the day has already declined." And he went in to stay with them.
verses.greek: καὶ παρεβιάσαντο αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Μεῖνον μεθ’ ἡμῶν, ὅτι πρὸς ἑσπέραν ἐστὶν καὶ κέκλικεν ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα. καὶ εἰσῆλθεν τοῦ μεῖναι σὺν αὐτοῖς.

verses.english: And it happened, as he reclined at table with them, that taking the loaf he blessed it, and breaking it he was giving it to them;
verses.greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ κατακλιθῆναι αὐτὸν μετ’ αὐτῶν λαβὼν τὸν ἄρτον εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἐπεδίδου αὐτοῖς·

verses.english: and their eyes were opened wide, and they recognised him; and he became invisible to them.
verses.greek: αὐτῶν δὲ διηνοίχθησαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν· καὶ αὐτὸς ἄφαντος ἐγένετο ἀπ’ αὐτῶν.

verses.english: And as they were speaking these things, he himself stood in the middle of them, and says to them, "Peace to you."
verses.greek: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτῶν λαλούντων αὐτὸς ἔστη ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.

verses.english: But being terrified and becoming afraid, they were thinking that they were seeing a spirit.
verses.greek: πτοηθέντες δὲ καὶ ἔμφοβοι γενόμενοι ἐδόκουν πνεῦμα θεωρεῖν.

verses.english: And he said to them, "Why are you troubled, and why do reasonings go up in your heart?
verses.greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί τεταραγμένοι ἐστέ, καὶ διὰ τί διαλογισμοὶ ἀναβαίνουσιν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν;

verses.english: See my hands and my feet, that I am he myself; because a spirit does not have bones, as you see me having."
verses.greek: ἴδετε τὰς χεῖράς μου καὶ τοὺς πόδας μου ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι αὐτός· ὅτι πνεῦμα ὀστέα οὐκ ἔχει καθὼς ἐμὲ θεωρεῖτε ἔχοντα.

verses.english: And having said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
verses.greek: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἔδειξεν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας.

verses.english: And while they were still not trusting for joy, and marvelling, he said to them, "Have you anything to eat here?"
verses.greek: ἔτι δὲ ἀπιστούντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς καὶ θαυμαζόντων εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἔχετέ τι βρώσιμον ἐνθάδε;

verses.english: And they gave him a piece of broiled fish;
verses.greek: οἱ δὲ ἐπέδωκαν αὐτῷ ἰχθύος ὀπτοῦ μέρος·

verses.english: and taking it, he ate it before them.
verses.greek: καὶ λαβὼν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ἔφαγεν.

verses.english: … and that a change of mind for release of sins should be proclaimed upon his name to all the nations.
verses.greek: … καὶ κηρυχθῆναι ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ μετάνοιαν εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη.

notes.explanation: Tertullian (4.43.1–5) follows the women who came "before light" with spices, the body not found, the two "messengers", the women's return "from the tomb" and the learners' persisting unbelief; he quotes the words of the two men: "Remember all that he told you in Galilee, that the son of the human must be delivered and crucified and on the third day rise." Epiphanius (sch. 76) quotes "Why do you seek the Living One among the dead? He has been raised. Remember all that he spoke to you while he was still with you." Two readings of this text are printed in 24:6: "all that" (ὅσα, both witnesses) and "he has been raised" without "he is not here, but" (Epiphanius, against his own habit of citation). "Of the Lord Jesus" (24:3) and "into the hands of sinful humans" (24:7) are not cited and are printed with NA27.

Tertullian (4.43.3–5): two of them were travelling; the Lord joined them without showing who he was, and even pretended not to know what had happened; they said "we thought that he was the redeemer of Israel", and he rebuked them: "O foolish and slow of heart to believe all that he spoke to you." Epiphanius (sch. 77) names Cleopas and states that the text read "that I spoke to you" where canonical Luke has "that the prophets spoke", and quotes "was it not necessary that he suffer these things?" and the opening of their eyes when he broke the bread. Both witnesses agree that the rebuke was about Jesus' own words, not about the prophets. Tertullian's "we thought" and "he spoke to you" are printed. "A prophet, powerful in deed and word" (24:19b) is not cited by either witness; it stands in the text as part of an attested verse.

Tertullian (4.43.6–8) quotes: "Why are you troubled, and why do thoughts arise in your hearts? See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself, for a spirit does not have bones as you see me having", and adds that Jesus asked for food "to show that he had teeth". Epiphanius (sch. 78) quotes the same verse with "bones" only. In this text there is no "handle me and see" and no "flesh and". Tertullian reports how Marcion read the end of the verse: "as you see me having" refers to the spirit, that is, "not having bones, as a spirit has none" (4.43.7). Eznik reports that the Marcionites based their abstinence from fish on Jesus' eating fish after his resurrection (De Deo 407, as quoted by Roth). "Peace to you" (24:36) and the showing of hands and feet (24:40), both lacking in D and the Old Latin, are not cited and are printed in grey.

No witness cites Peter's visit to the tomb (24:12) or the report of it (24:24); both are classed probably absent, since the linen cloths would have served Tertullian's argument and 24:12 is also lacking in D and the Old Latin. The interpretation of "Moses and all the prophets" (24:27), the burning hearts "while he opened to us the scriptures" (24:32) and "everything written about me in the law of Moses and the prophets and the psalms" with the opening of their minds (24:44–46) would have been Tertullian's proof that Jesus is the Christ of the prophets, the thesis with which he ends his book; neither witness cites them, and they are classed probably absent. The return to Jerusalem and the appearance to Simon (24:33–35) form a paragraph with no attested verse. Nothing after 24:47 is cited.

Tertullian ends his commentary on the gospel with Jesus "sending the emissaries to preach to all the nations" (4.43.9). Whether the text went on, and how (the parting at Bethany, 24:50–51, or an ending like Acts 1:8–11), is not attested; the text is printed to the last attested verse. In canonical Luke 24:47 is governed by "thus it is written" (24:46); the words that introduced it in this text are not known.

Interpretation. Three layers are kept apart. (a) Text: the two men at the tomb call Jesus "the Living One" and say "he has been raised"; the learners recognize him in the breaking of the bread; he answers their fear of a spirit by showing hands and feet and saying that a spirit does not have bones "as you see me having"; he asks for food; he sends them to all the nations; the rebuke on the road is about believing his own words. (b) Canonical Luke has in addition the touch and the flesh (24:39), Peter at the tomb and the appearance to Simon (24:12, 24, 34), and the proof from Moses, the prophets and the psalms with the commissioning of the Eleven (24:27, 32, 44–49). On the Semler model these are a common original's; on the Schwegler model, additions; the witnesses show only that the text attested here lacked them. (c) Reception: the Marcionites read 24:39 as Jesus saying that he had no bones, like a spirit (Tertullian 4.43.7), and kept the meal of fish as the basis of their own practice (Eznik). The text itself holds together the Living One who is not found among the dead and a risen Jesus who can be seen, who eats, and who is recognized at table.

notes.term: τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων, "on the first of the week"
notes.explanation: Literally "on the one of the sabbaths". σάββατα, plural, is also the week, as at 18:12.
Very early, at first light. βαθύς, "deep", is the word of 5:4 and 6:48.

notes.term: τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, "of the lord Jesus"
notes.explanation: The wording of NA27 here. κύριος in lower case, as at 7:13.
Not knowing which way to turn.
ἀνήρ, men. The text calls them men; in 24:23 the women speak of "messengers".
As at 20:1.
Flashing like lightning, as at 9:29.
κλίνω, as at 9:58.
The participle of ζάω, "to live", with the article: "the one who lives".
ἐγείρω, passive, as at 7:16 and 9:7. This text lacks "he is not here, but".

notes.term: ὅσα ἐλάλησεν ὑμῖν, "all that he spoke to you"
notes.explanation: The reading of this text, ὅσα, "all that". Canonical Luke has ὡς, "how".
As at 9:22.
As at 9:44.
ἀνίστημι, the verb of ἀνάστασις (20:27).
ῥῆμα, as at 5:5.
As at 8:2.

notes.term: Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου, "Mary the mother of Jacob"
notes.explanation: The Greek says only "Mary of Jacob": mother, wife or daughter is not said. "Mother" is the usual reading.
As at 6:13.
Nonsense, silly talk.
ἀπιστέω, the opposite of πιστεύω.
A stadion was about 185 metres: about eleven kilometres.
To converse.
The road verb with συν-, "together".
κρατέω, to hold, seize, as at 8:54.

notes.term: τοῦ μὴ ἐπιγνῶναι, "so that they did not recognise"
notes.explanation: ἐπιγινώσκω, to recognise, know fully.
To throw back and forth.
Sad-faced, gloomy.
To live as a stranger, sojourn.
As at 4:34.

notes.term: ἀνὴρ προφήτης δυνατός, "a man, a prophet, powerful"
notes.explanation: ἀνήρ, a man.

notes.term: εἰς κρίμα θανάτου, "to a sentence of death"
notes.explanation: κρίμα, a judgement, a sentence.
The reading of this text, from Tertullian's putabamus (a retroversion). Canonical Luke has ἠλπίζομεν, "we were hoping".
λυτρόω, to set free by paying a ransom. "Redeem" is the Latin term for the same thing.

notes.term: τρίτην ταύτην ἡμέραν ἄγει, "this is the third day"
notes.explanation: Literally "it is passing this third day".
As at 8:56.
Early in the morning.
ἄγγελος, as at 9:26.
ζάω, as in "the Living One" (24:5).
Without νοῦς, mind: as at 6:11.
Slow, sluggish.

notes.term: ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐλάλησεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, "in all that he spoke to you"
notes.explanation: The reading of this text, from Epiphanius. Canonical Luke has "in all that the prophets spoke".
δεῖ, as at 9:22.

notes.term: εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, "go into his glory"
notes.explanation: δόξα, as at 9:26.
To pretend, act as if.
To urge strongly, compel.
κλίνω, as at 9:12.
As at 7:36.
εὐλογέω, as at 9:16.
The imperfect, as at 9:16.
διανοίγω, to open fully.
ἄφαντος, unseen.
The present tense, kept.
The Hebrew greeting shalom lakhem.
πνεῦμα, spirit, also breath and wind.
Stirred up, disturbed.
διαλογισμός, as at 5:22; ἀναβαίνω, to go up, as at 9:28 and 18:10.

notes.term: ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι αὐτός, "that I am he myself"
notes.explanation: Literally "that I am myself".

notes.term: πνεῦμα ὀστέα οὐκ ἔχει καθὼς ἐμὲ θεωρεῖτε ἔχοντα, "a spirit does not have bones, as you see me having"
notes.explanation: This text lacks "handle me and see" and "flesh and". The Greek of the second clause can be grouped two ways: "as you see that I have", or "[does not have bones] as you see me [not] having". The Marcionite reading took it the second way (Tertullian, Marc. 4.43.7). The English keeps the Greek order, which allows both.

notes.term: ἀπιστούντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς, "still not trusting for joy"
notes.explanation: ἀπιστέω, as at 24:11.
Anything edible.

notes.term: ἰχθύος ὀπτοῦ μέρος, "a piece of broiled fish"
notes.explanation: ὀπτός, roasted, broiled.
The printed text begins inside a sentence. The words before it (24:46, "thus it is written that…") are not printed, and the verse depends on them. The ellipsis marks this.

notes.term: μετάνοιαν εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν, "a change of mind for release of sins"
notes.explanation: μετάνοια, as at 5:32; ἄφεσις, release, as at 5:20. The last line of the text uses the two words.

notes.term: ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ, "upon his name"
notes.explanation: As at 21:8.

notes.term: εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, "to all the nations"
notes.explanation: ἔθνη, as at 12:30.
